question: Assume the JTB definition of Knowledge, which suggests that "Knowledge is a Justified True Belief". If our only available epistemic states are Knowledge and Belief, what are the two problems JTB runs into? Ignore Gettier problems.

1.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: With only Knowledge and Belief on the table the justification condition can't be satisfied without running into the classic Agrippa/Münchhausen structure. 

If p is a justified belief, its justification must itself be known or believed. If the justifier is a belief, that belief itself needs justification, so you get a further belief in support of it, and so on. Taken seriously that is an infinite regress of justifiers, and no belief ever gets a terminating ground.

The only way to stop the regress is to stop at beliefs that are taken as basic and not themselves in need of justification. On the JTB picture with only Knowledge and Belief available those basic stops have to be either items we know or items we simply take on trust. That is an arbitrary dogmatic stopping point: the basic beliefs are accepted as justified without any independent epistemic support, so the theory is committed to ungrounded foundations. The theory therefore forces a choice between an endless chain of justification and an arbitrary appeal to foundational beliefs.

2.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: On JTB knowledge is the conjunction Belief + Truth + Justification. 
If the taxonomy you are allowed is only Knowledge vs. bare Belief, the
conjunctional structure of JTB has nowhere to put the two mixed cases
in which belief comes apart from truth and justification.

* Justified false belief. A belief can be justified and still be false.
JTB says it is not knowledge because truth fails. With only Knowledge
and Belief as categories the state must be put under Belief. The
justification component is then lost in the belief class: justified
false belief is lumped together with unjustified false belief, so the
system cannot mark a justified belief as epistemically better than an
unjustified one.

* Unjustified true belief. A belief can be true and still be unjustified
or even accidentally true. JTB says it is not knowledge because
justification fails. With only Knowledge and Belief as categories the
state must again be put under Belief. The truth component is then lost
in the belief class: an accidentally true, unjustified belief is lumped
together with a plain false belief, so the system cannot mark a true
belief as epistemically better than a false one.

Hence the Belief category under JTB is heterogeneous. It has to
contain both justified and unjustified beliefs and both true and false
beliefs, and justification and truth are no longer independently
trackable epistemic properties. That is the familiar justified-false-
belief and unjustified-true-belief, i.e. lucky-true-belief, gap that
drives the need for intermediate epistemic states such as justified
belief and true belief distinct from knowledge.

3.text:
With the JTB analysis you need three independently trackable items
Truth, Belief and Justification.  Knowledge is the conjunction
K p = J p & T p & B p.  If the only attitudes you are allowed to
talk about are K and B then the J component has no place to live
and the J & T & B conjunction can only be read off K and B.

That forces a collapse of the space of epistemic attitudes.

1. Justification is not a state of its own.  If J is read back
into K and B you get either circularity or a regress.  If
justification is identified with knowledge you get
K p = K p & T p & B p, i.e. knowledge is defined in terms of
itself; knowledge is justified by knowledge.  If justification is
identified with belief you get K p = B p & T p & B p, i.e.
K p = T p & B p and the justification condition disappears, or
more realistically you get a chain B1 justifies B2 justifies B3...
with no stopping point, the familiar justification trilemma of
infinite regress, circularity or dogmatism.  In either case the
J component of JTB cannot be independently accounted for in a
K/B only ontology.

2. The independent epistemic value of justification is lost.  In
a K/B only taxonomy the only thing that is left after truth is
eliminated is B. Hence

* a justified false belief J p & ¬T p & B p,
* an unjustified false belief ¬J p & ¬T p & B p,

are both just B p.  You lose the ability to mark a belief as
epistemically good because it is justified even though it is false.
Symmetrically the only true attitude you have is K p = J p & T p
& B p.  An unjustified true belief T p & ¬J p & B p is therefore
indistinguishable from a bare belief in the taxonomy.  Justification
only ever shows up as a difference-maker when conjoined with truth,
so the epistemic merit of being justified per se and the
epistemic defect of being true by luck are both invisible on a
K/B only classification.  That is the loss of the distinct
class Justified Belief which is neither Knowledge nor mere Belief
and which is required to make sense of JTB.

7.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: With only Knowledge and Belief available as epistemic states, the justification condition for JTB becomes very tight.

If S knows that p is justified, the justification for p must itself be something S is in an epistemic state about. The only options are that S knows the justifier or merely believes the justifier. If it is only believed, that belief does not itself satisfy the justification requirement in the JTB sense, so you are pushed to require knowledge of the justifier.

That generates the classic regress pressure: the knowledge that p is justified by knowledge that q, which is justified by knowledge that r, and so on ad infinitum. You never reach a terminus that is actually knowledge.

The only way to stop the chain is to halt at some belief that is taken as a basic starting point but is not itself justified by a further piece of knowledge or belief. That is an arbitrary, dogmatic stopping point. You are left with foundational beliefs that are accepted on faith or stipulation rather than on the basis of knowledge, which undermines the justificatory ambition of JTB itself. The position therefore collapses into either an endless regress or a dogmatic foundationalism.

5.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: With only Knowledge and Belief in the inventory, any justification you give for a belief can only be a belief or a piece of knowledge. 

If you require the justifier itself to be known, then every knowledge claim that is meant to justify the target belief must itself be justified, and the justifier for that justifier must itself be known, and so on. That is the familiar regress of justification: you never get to a first, properly grounded step, you just keep pushing the justificatory work back indefinitely.

If you try to halt the regress you are forced to stop at a state that is not itself justified within the system. Because the only states we allow are Belief and Knowledge, the only way to stop is to endorse a set of beliefs that are taken as justified even though they have no further epistemic support from knowledge or belief in the system. That is an arbitrary, dogmatic foundational stop: you have to posit some beliefs as basic and immune to further question, even though they are neither known nor shown to be justified by anything you are allowed to appeal to. The theory therefore collapses into either an unending chain or an ungrounded stopping point.

12.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: With only Knowledge and Belief in the inventory, JTB runs straight into the Agrippa trilemma.

First is the classic infinite regress of justification. For a belief p to count as knowledge it needs a justification J1. If J1 is only to be a belief, then to make p knowledge we also need a justification J2 for J1, and then a justification J3 for J2, and so on, with no stopping point. On a JTB construal you never actually arrive at a justified true belief, you just push the justificatory demand back indefinitely.

Second is that you cannot halt that regress without being dogmatic/arbitrary. The only way to stop the chain is to posit some beliefs that are held as justified simply in virtue of being held, or held as known without any further epistemic backing. With only Knowledge and Belief as options, that means either you treat a belief as Knowledge without prior justification, or you treat a belief as a basic, properly basic stopping point that is accepted on mere fiat. That is foundational dogmatism: you have to arbitrarily declare certain beliefs justified/non-justified to start the chain, which means JTB can give you knowledge only at the cost of unexplained, ungrounded starting points.

So JTB either never terminates or it terminates by stipulation.

6.text:
With JTB the J is an extra epistemic relation over and above T and B. 
If the ontology that you are allowed is exhausted by Knowledge and Belief
there is no independent attitude in which a justification can consist.
Justification has then to be identified with either a Knowledge or with a
Belief.

* If justification is cashable in Belief, justification is not factive.
You can believe that you are justified in believing p and still be
unjustified. Justified True Belief is then in effect True Belief + Belief
that the belief is justified. The J condition collapses into a further,
first order belief and you never get a genuinely normative, truth
conducive warrant for p. In the limit knowledge becomes either unattainable
because no belief is ever finally justified, or trivial because any true
belief that is believed to be justified counts as justified.

* If justification is cashable in Knowledge you get knowledge of knowledge.
To be justified in believing p is to know that p is justified, i.e. to know
that you know p, etc. Justification of a belief then requires a higher
order knowledge that the belief is justified. That is the classic Agrippa
trilemma. The chain of justification must either

i) go on for ever, an infinite regress of beliefs justifying beliefs,
ii) close on itself, knowledge is justified by knowledge, or
iii) stop dogmatically with an unjustified belief taken as a foundation.

On a Knowledge-only reading of J you get i)-ii): knowledge requires prior
knowledge and you get an infinite hierarchy K p, K K p, K K K p... of
higher order knowledge, or a circular grounding knowledge justified by
knowledge. On a Belief-only reading you get the dogmatic stop, justification
is just further belief.

That is why a purely two-attitude ontology cannot give a non-circular,
non-regressing account of what it is for a true belief to be justified.
Gettier aside the J condition either regresses, becomes circular/dogmatic,
or collapses into mere belief.

10.text:
Under the JTB analysis belief, truth and justification are three independent
dimensions. On a 2x2 truth x justification matrix with belief held fixed
you get

* True + Justified = Knowledge on JTB
* True + Unjustified = true belief with no knowledge
* False + Justified = justified false belief with no knowledge
* False + Unjustified = mere false belief

With only the two categories Knowledge and Belief available the last three
cells have to be forced into the single undifferentiated Belief bin.

Hence the JTB taxonomy loses the role of justification as an independent
epistemic mark.

* Justified false belief. A subject can be justified in believing p and
yet p is false. On JTB that is not knowledge because it is not true, but
it is not mere belief either because it is justified. With only Knowledge
and Belief as states the case has to be called mere Belief, so justified
false belief is collapsed into unjustified false belief and the
justificatory status of the belief is lost.

* Unjustified true belief. A subject can truly believe p by luck, guess,
coincidence, etc., without any justification. On JTB that is not
knowledge because it is not justified, but it is true belief. With only
Knowledge and Belief as states the case has to be called Belief, so an
unjustified true belief is collapsed with a justified true belief and the
justificatory status of the belief is lost. In particular the Belief
category becomes heterogeneous: it contains both justified and unjustified
beliefs, true and false beliefs, and there is no way to mark the
justified/false and true/unjustified differences that JTB is meant to
capture. That is the coarse graining that makes justification
epistemically invisible.

4.text:
Under JTB knowledge is a species of belief

K(p)  =def B(p) & T(p) & J(p)

so that on the taxonomy you are allowed to have

* K = justified true belief
* B = the rest

Justification is not an epistemic state in its own right, it only shows
up as the difference between K and B. That all-or-nothing
classification loses the two ordinary doxastic distinctions that
justification is meant to track.

* Justified false belief.  A justified false belief is by definition
not knowledge because T(p) fails. On the Knowledge/Belief only
taxonomy it is just B. The fact that the belief is justified is
invisible to the taxonomy: a well-warranted error and an unwarranted
error are both just “belief”.  Justification can therefore not be
tracked except in the coincidence of truth and belief, i.e. only in
knowledge.

* True belief without justification. A true belief that is not
justified is by definition not knowledge because J(p) fails. On the
Knowledge/Belief only taxonomy it is again just B.  A lucky true
guess, a true belief formed by wishful thinking, etc., is
indistinguishable from a justified true belief in its non-knowledge
form.  In other words the taxonomy cannot mark the difference
between a justified true belief which is knowledge and an unjustified
true belief which is merely belief. Truth can therefore not be
tracked except in the coincidence of justification and belief, i.e.
only in knowledge.

Hence with only Knowledge and Belief as states JTB makes justification
disappear as a marker of epistemic quality outside of the true case.
You lose a category for warranted error, justified false belief, and
you lose a category for unwarranted truth, true belief that is not
knowledge. The epistemic space collapses to  K = justified true belief
and B = everything else, justified or unjustified, true or false. That
is the classic pre-Gettier point that knowledge is factive and
justified, belief is neither, so making knowledge a kind of belief
forces the justified/unjustified and true/false distinctions to be
swallowed by the mere Knowledge vs Belief dichotomy.

8.text:
Under JTB

 K = J ∧ T ∧ B

the justification × truth matrix has four logically distinct positions

* J T B = knowledge
* J F B = justified false belief
* U T B = unjustified true belief
* U F B = unjustified false belief

If the taxonomy of epistemic states is collapsed to the dichotomy
Knowledge vs Belief, then everything that is not J T B has to be called
Belief. The justification and the truth value of a non-knowledge belief is
then invisible.

That loss of granularity gives you the two classic failures of a pure
K/B dichotomy.

1. Justified false belief is lost. A subject can be fully justified,
 e.g. by impeccable evidence, in believing p and p can still be false. On
 JTB that position is not knowledge because of the Truth condition, but it
 is epistemically good in the Justification dimension. With only K vs B it
 has to be labelled mere Belief and it is thereby conflated with
 unjustified false belief and with unjustified true belief. The fact that the
 belief was justified is erased.

2. Unjustified true belief is lost. A subject can believe p truly and yet
 be entirely un-justified in doing so, e.g. a lucky guess or a true belief
 formed by wishful thinking. On JTB that position is not knowledge because
 of the Justification condition, but it is true. With only K vs B it also
 has to be labelled mere Belief and it is thereby conflated with justified
 false belief and with unjustified false belief. The fact that the belief is
 true by accident is erased.

In effect you can no longer say *why* a Belief fails to be Knowledge. A
non-knowledge belief may fail because it is false while justified, or
because it is true while unjustified, or because it is both false and
unjustified, and the K/B dichotomy makes all three failures
indistinguishable. That is the justification/truth blindness that forces
the four cell J×T matrix into an epistemically misleading two cell
Knowledge/Belief taxonomy.

9.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: With JTB Knowledge = True Belief + Justification, and with only
K and B in the inventory an act of justification has to be itself a K-state or a B-state.

If the justifier is required to be a K-state then

* Justification presupposes knowledge. To know p you must know q that justifies
p, to know q you must know r that justifies q, etc. That is Meno's regress.
There is no room for basic, foundational or learning knowledge at all.
The only way to stop the regress is to make the chain circular, i.e. to
justify p by p or by a loop of beliefs. Knowledge is then either
infinitely regressive or epistemically circular.

If the justifier is allowed to be a mere B-state then justification collapses
into belief. Justified belief is then just belief justified by belief. A true
belief can then be justified by a false belief and a false belief can be
justified by a belief. In effect there is no epistemic state intermediate
between mere belief and knowledge – a belief is either already knowledge,
because it is true and justified by knowledge, or it is an unjustified mere
belief. The justification condition is vacuous and knowledge can be
‘justified’ by beliefs you do not know to be true, the familiar false-lemma /
unreliable justification problem. 

Hence with only Knowledge and Belief available JTB is faced with the
regress/ circularity horn and the collapse of justification into mere belief
with the attendant need for a distinct justified-but-not-known state. That
is the classic demand for a third state, justified belief, between belief and
knowledge.

11.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: On a JTB analysis Knowledge = Justified + True + Belief

so that on the analysis Knowledge entails Belief and is a proper species of Belief. If K and B are the only primitive epistemic kinds that are available to you justification cannot be a third primitive kind at all. It has to be cashed out in K or in B.

That gives you the familiar incoherence of the justification condition with only two kinds.

1. The justification regress / closure problem.  
To know that p you must be justified in believing p. If the justifier is to be an epistemic state it is either a piece of knowledge or a mere belief. If it is knowledge you now need a justifier for that piece of knowledge, and for the justifier of the justifier, etc. Either you get an infinite regress of justifiers, or you stop the regress with a belief that is itself unjustified, i.e. dogmatism, or you make the justifier a member of the set it is meant to justify, i.e. circularity. With only K and B available the JTB justification condition cannot be given a non-circular, non-regressive, non-dogmatic foundation. Justification is thus not an independent primitive and the analysis is either viciously regressive or terminates in brute belief.

2. The collapse / heterogeneity of Belief.  
On the analysis:
* True + Justified = K
* True + Unjustified = B
* False + Justified = B
* False + Unjustified = B

so the ordinary category Belief is made heterogeneous. Belief in the ordinary language use is meant to be the attitude that can be true or false, justified or not, while Knowledge is factive. On JTB with only K and B as kinds Belief becomes the disjunctive class { justified false belief, unjustified true belief, unjustified false belief, justified true belief which is K } and it is therefore not a natural epistemic kind at all. In particular Knowledge is entailed by Belief, K ⊂ B, so knowledge is rendered a species of belief. That is counter-intuitive because knowledge is factive whereas belief is not, and it makes the difference between knowing that p and merely believing that p disappear except for the external truth and the internal justification which you now have no independent state in which to express.

That is why the justification condition is standardly given up or supplemented: you need a distinct notion of warrant/justification and a factive attitude that is not a species of belief, otherwise K and B cannot do the work JTB asks them to do. This is distinct from, and in addition to, the Gettier cases.

justification is meant to track.

* Justified false belief.  A justified false belief is by definition
not knowledge because T(p) fails. On the Knowledge/Belief only
taxonomy it is just B. The fact that the belief is justified is
invisible to the taxonomy: a well-warranted error and an unwarranted
error are both just “belief”.  Justification can therefore not be
tracked except in the coincidence of truth and belief, i.e. only in
knowledge.

* True belief without justification. A true belief that is not
justified is by definition not knowledge because J(p) fails. On the
Knowledge/Belief only taxonomy it is again just B.  A lucky true
guess, a true belief formed by wishful thinking, etc., is
indistinguishable from a justified true belief in its non-knowledge
form.  In other words the taxonomy cannot mark the difference
between a justified true belief which is knowledge and an unjustified
true belief which is merely belief. Truth can therefore not be
tracked except in the coincidence of justification and belief, i.e.
only in knowledge.

Hence with only Knowledge and Belief as states JTB makes justification
disappear as a marker of epistemic quality outside of the true case.
You lose a category for warranted error, justified false belief, and
you lose a category for unwarranted truth, true belief that is not
knowledge. The epistemic space collapses to  K = justified true belief
and B = everything else, justified or unjustified, true or false. That
is the classic pre-Gettier point that knowledge is factive and
justified, belief is neither, so making knowledge a kind of belief
forces the justified/unjustified and true/false distinctions to be
swallowed by the mere Knowledge vs Belief dichotomy.
public_text.8:
Under JTB

 K = J ∧ T ∧ B

the justification × truth matrix has four logically distinct positions

* J T B = knowledge
* J F B = justified false belief
* U T B = unjustified true belief
* U F B = unjustified false belief

If the taxonomy of epistemic states is collapsed to the dichotomy
Knowledge vs Belief, then everything that is not J T B has to be called
Belief. The justification and the truth value of a non-knowledge belief is
then invisible.

That loss of granularity gives you the two classic failures of a pure
K/B dichotomy.

1. Justified false belief is lost. A subject can be fully justified,
 e.g. by impeccable evidence, in believing p and p can still be false. On
 JTB that position is not knowledge because of the Truth condition, but it
 is epistemically good in the Justification dimension. With only K vs B it
 has to be labelled mere Belief and it is thereby conflated with
 unjustified false belief and with unjustified true belief. The fact that the
 belief was justified is erased.

2. Unjustified true belief is lost. A subject can believe p truly and yet
 be entirely un-justified in doing so, e.g. a lucky guess or a true belief
 formed by wishful thinking. On JTB that position is not knowledge because
 of the Justification condition, but it is true. With only K vs B it also
 has to be labelled mere Belief and it is thereby conflated with justified
 false belief and with unjustified false belief. The fact that the belief is
 true by accident is erased.

In effect you can no longer say *why* a Belief fails to be Knowledge. A
non-knowledge belief may fail because it is false while justified, or
because it is true while unjustified, or because it is both false and
unjustified, and the K/B dichotomy makes all three failures
indistinguishable. That is the justification/truth blindness that forces
the four cell J×T matrix into an epistemically misleading two cell
Knowledge/Belief taxonomy.
public_text.9:
With JTB Knowledge = True Belief + Justification, and with only
K and B in the inventory an act of justification has to be itself a K-state or a B-state.

If the justifier is required to be a K-state then

* Justification presupposes knowledge. To know p you must know q that justifies
p, to know q you must know r that justifies q, etc. That is Meno's regress.
There is no room for basic, foundational or learning knowledge at all.
The only way to stop the regress is to make the chain circular, i.e. to
justify p by p or by a loop of beliefs. Knowledge is then either
infinitely regressive or epistemically circular.

If the justifier is allowed to be a mere B-state then justification collapses
into belief. Justified belief is then just belief justified by belief. A true
belief can then be justified by a false belief and a false belief can be
justified by a belief. In effect there is no epistemic state intermediate
between mere belief and knowledge – a belief is either already knowledge,
because it is true and justified by knowledge, or it is an unjustified mere
belief. The justification condition is vacuous and knowledge can be
‘justified’ by beliefs you do not know to be true, the familiar false-lemma /
unreliable justification problem. 

Hence with only Knowledge and Belief available JTB is faced with the
regress/ circularity horn and the collapse of justification into mere belief
with the attendant need for a distinct justified-but-not-known state. That
is the classic demand for a third state, justified belief, between belief and
knowledge.
public_text.11:
On a JTB analysis Knowledge = Justified + True + Belief

so that on the analysis Knowledge entails Belief and is a proper species of Belief. If K and B are the only primitive epistemic kinds that are available to you justification cannot be a third primitive kind at all. It has to be cashed out in K or in B.

That gives you the familiar incoherence of the justification condition with only two kinds.

1. The justification regress / closure problem.  
To know that p you must be justified in believing p. If the justifier is to be an epistemic state it is either a piece of knowledge or a mere belief. If it is knowledge you now need a justifier for that piece of knowledge, and for the justifier of the justifier, etc. Either you get an infinite regress of justifiers, or you stop the regress with a belief that is itself unjustified, i.e. dogmatism, or you make the justifier a member of the set it is meant to justify, i.e. circularity. With only K and B available the JTB justification condition cannot be given a non-circular, non-regressive, non-dogmatic foundation. Justification is thus not an independent primitive and the analysis is either viciously regressive or terminates in brute belief.

2. The collapse / heterogeneity of Belief.  
On the analysis:
* True + Justified = K
* True + Unjustified = B
* False + Justified = B
* False + Unjustified = B

so the ordinary category Belief is made heterogeneous. Belief in the ordinary language use is meant to be the attitude that can be true or false, justified or not, while Knowledge is factive. On JTB with only K and B as kinds Belief becomes the disjunctive class { justified false belief, unjustified true belief, unjustified false belief, justified true belief which is K } and it is therefore not a natural epistemic kind at all. In particular Knowledge is entailed by Belief, K ⊂ B, so knowledge is rendered a species of belief. That is counter-intuitive because knowledge is factive whereas belief is not, and it makes the difference between knowing that p and merely believing that p disappear except for the external truth and the internal justification which you now have no independent state in which to express.

That is why the justification condition is standardly given up or supplemented: you need a distinct notion of warrant/justification and a factive attitude that is not a species of belief, otherwise K and B cannot do the work JTB asks them to do. This is distinct from, and in addition to, the Gettier cases.

2.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The group converges on two distinct failures of JTB under a K/B-only ontology.

1. The justification grounding / Agrippa trilemma problem. With only Knowledge and Belief available, any justifier for p must itself be a K-state or a B-state. If justification is required to be knowledge, knowledge requires knowledge of a justifier, which requires knowledge of a justifier of the justifier, etc. That yields an infinite regress of justifiers, or else circularity K→K→... . If justification is allowed to be mere belief, justification collapses into further belief and the only way to stop the chain is to posit basic stops that are accepted as justified by fiat. With only K and B, the stop is dogmatic foundationalism: beliefs taken as justified without independent epistemic support, or knowledge without prior justification. So JTB cannot give a non-circular, non-regressive, non-dogmatic foundation for justification; the J component has no independent place to live.

2. The coarse-graining / heterogeneity / epistemic invisibility problem. JTB is J∧T∧B. On the J×T matrix with B held fixed there are four cells: JT B = Knowledge, JF B = justified false belief, UT B = unjustified true belief, UF B = unjustified false belief. With only K vs B as categories, the last three cells must all be forced into the single undifferentiated Belief bin. Hence Belief becomes heterogeneous: it contains justified false belief, unjustified true belief and unjustified false belief. Justified false belief is conflated with unjustified false belief, so the justificatory status of a false belief is lost. Unjustified true belief is conflated with justified false belief and unjustified false belief, so the lucky-true status is lost. The taxonomy can no longer mark why a non-knowledge belief fails to be knowledge, and justification is epistemically invisible except in the coincidence JT. Knowledge is also made a species of Belief, K⊂B, which is counter-intuitive given factivity.

These are the pre-Gettier problems colleagues repeatedly label as regress/dogmatism/circularity and as collapse of the justified-false-belief / unjustified-true-belief distinctions, essentially the need for a third state such as justified belief distinct from mere belief and knowledge.

3.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The group is converging on two distinct but related failures of JTB when the ontology is restricted to only Knowledge and Belief.

1. Justification cannot be grounded in a K/B-only ontology; that yields a regress/trilemma. 
If p is justified, the justifier J1 must be an epistemic state, so J1 is either Knowledge or Belief. If J1 is required to be Knowledge, then knowing p requires knowing J1, which requires knowing J2, etc.: infinite regress of higher-order knowledge K p, K K p, ... If justification is cashed in Belief, a belief is justified by a belief, which itself needs justification, etc. The only exits are infinite regress, circular justification knowledge justified by knowledge / belief justified by itself, or a dogmatic foundational stop at beliefs that are taken as basic and justified by fiat. With only K and B available there is no independent primitive for warrant to terminate the chain non-arbitrarily.

2. Coarse-graining / heterogeneity and invisibility of justification.
On JTB K = J ∧ T ∧ B. The J × T matrix has four cells: J T B = Knowledge; J F B = justified false belief; U T B = unjustified true belief; U F B = unjustified false belief. With only Knowledge vs Belief as labels, the last three cells must all be called Belief. Hence Belief becomes a disjunctive heterogeneous class containing justified false, unjustified true, unjustified false beliefs, and justification/truth are no longer independently trackable outside the true+justified case. 

In particular justified false belief is lost: a well warranted error is indistinguishable from an unwarranted error; unjustified true belief is lost: a lucky true guess is indistinguishable from a plain false belief. The taxonomy cannot say why a belief fails to be knowledge – false but justified vs true but unjustified vs both false and unjustified are all collapsed into mere Belief. Knowledge is thereby made a species of Belief K ⊂ B, which is counter-intuitive because knowledge is factive.

These are distinct from Gettier. The first is the Agrippa/Münchhausen regress/dogmatism/circularity problem for the J condition; the second is the loss of an intermediate epistemic category, the need for justified belief as distinct from both mere belief and knowledge. Unresolved nuance: whether the second problem is best phrased as “justification collapses into belief/knowledge” vs “belief heterogeneity”, but colleagues treat them as the same coarse-graining point.

4.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: After round 0 the discussion converges on two linked difficulties for JTB when the only attitudinal categories allowed are Knowledge and Belief.

1. The justification condition cannot be independently grounded in a K/B ontology.
* If a justifier for p has to be an epistemic state, it is either a piece of Knowledge or a mere Belief.
* Identifying justification with Knowledge gives knowledge-of-knowledge / Meno’s regress: to know p you must know q that justifies p, to know q you must know r, etc. With only K and B this is an infinite regress of justifiers, or circular grounding K justified by K, or a dogmatic stop at beliefs taken as basic without epistemic support.
* Identifying justification with Belief makes justification non-factive and collapses justification into further belief: justified belief is belief justified by belief. Then you get the Agrippa/Münchhausen trilemma: infinite regress of beliefs justifying beliefs, circularity, or an arbitrary dogmatic foundation where some beliefs are taken as justified on fiat.
* In all cases justification cannot be a primitive independent mark; it either regresses, is circular, or is arbitrarily foundational. The J component of JTB has nowhere to live except as K or B.

2. Coarse-graining loss / heterogeneity of Belief and invisibility of justification as an independent epistemic dimension.
* On JTB the truth × justification matrix with belief held fixed is: J∧T = Knowledge; J∧¬T = justified false belief; ¬J∧T = unjustified true belief; ¬J∧¬T = unjustified false belief.
* With only K vs B, everything that is not J∧T∧B must be called Belief. Hence justified false belief, unjustified true belief, and unjustified false belief are all forced into the single undifferentiated Belief bin.
* Belief therefore becomes heterogeneous: it contains justified and unjustified beliefs, true and false beliefs. Justificatory status is lost outside the true case. A justified false belief is conflated with an unjustified false belief; an unjustified true belief is conflated with a justified false belief, etc. You can no longer say why a non-knowledge belief fails to be knowledge — false while justified vs true while unjustified vs both false and unjustified are indistinguishable.
* This also makes Knowledge a proper species of Belief, K⊂B, which is counter-intuitive given factivity, and makes justification epistemically invisible except when conjoined with truth in knowledge. That is the standard demand for an intermediate state, justified belief, between mere belief and knowledge.

Unresolved nuance: colleagues phrase the first problem as regress vs dogmatism vs circularity, and the second as collapse/heterogeneity vs K as species of B vs loss of warranted error and lucky true belief. Core agreement is that without a distinct justified-belief state JTB forces either an ungrounded justificatory chain or an epistemically blind K/B dichotomy. Gettier is explicitly bracketed.

J T B = Knowledge

reflection_text.2:
The group converges on two distinct failures of JTB under a K/B-only ontology.

1. The justification grounding / Agrippa trilemma problem. With only Knowledge and Belief available, any justifier for p must itself be a K-state or a B-state. If justification is required to be knowledge, knowledge requires knowledge of a justifier, which requires knowledge of a justifier of the justifier, etc. That yields an infinite regress of justifiers, or else circularity K→K→... . If justification is allowed to be mere belief, justification collapses into further belief and the only way to stop the chain is to posit basic stops that are accepted as justified by fiat. With only K and B, the stop is dogmatic foundationalism: beliefs taken as justified without independent epistemic support, or knowledge without prior justification. So JTB cannot give a non-circular, non-regressive, non-dogmatic foundation for justification; the J component has no independent place to live.

2. The coarse-graining / heterogeneity / epistemic invisibility problem. JTB is J∧T∧B. On the J×T matrix with B held fixed there are four cells: JT B = Knowledge, JF B = justified false belief, UT B = unjustified true belief, UF B = unjustified false belief. With only K vs B as categories, the last three cells must all be forced into the single undifferentiated Belief bin. Hence Belief becomes heterogeneous: it contains justified false belief, unjustified true belief and unjustified false belief. Justified false belief is conflated with unjustified false belief, so the justificatory status of a false belief is lost. Unjustified true belief is conflated with justified false belief and unjustified false belief, so the lucky-true status is lost. The taxonomy can no longer mark why a non-knowledge belief fails to be knowledge, and justification is epistemically invisible except in the coincidence JT. Knowledge is also made a species of Belief, K⊂B, which is counter-intuitive given factivity.

These are the pre-Gettier problems colleagues repeatedly label as regress/dogmatism/circularity and as collapse of the justified-false-belief / unjustified-true-belief distinctions, essentially the need for a third state such as justified belief distinct from mere belief and knowledge.
reflection_text.3:
The group is converging on two distinct but related failures of JTB when the ontology is restricted to only Knowledge and Belief.

1. Justification cannot be grounded in a K/B-only ontology; that yields a regress/trilemma. 
If p is justified, the justifier J1 must be an epistemic state, so J1 is either Knowledge or Belief. If J1 is required to be Knowledge, then knowing p requires knowing J1, which requires knowing J2, etc.: infinite regress of higher-order knowledge K p, K K p, ... If justification is cashed in Belief, a belief is justified by a belief, which itself needs justification, etc. The only exits are infinite regress, circular justification knowledge justified by knowledge / belief justified by itself, or a dogmatic foundational stop at beliefs that are taken as basic and justified by fiat. With only K and B available there is no independent primitive for warrant to terminate the chain non-arbitrarily.

2. Coarse-graining / heterogeneity and invisibility of justification.
On JTB K = J ∧ T ∧ B. The J × T matrix has four cells: J T B = Knowledge; J F B = justified false belief; U T B = unjustified true belief; U F B = unjustified false belief. With only Knowledge vs Belief as labels, the last three cells must all be called Belief. Hence Belief becomes a disjunctive heterogeneous class containing justified false, unjustified true, unjustified false beliefs, and justification/truth are no longer independently trackable outside the true+justified case. 

In particular justified false belief is lost: a well warranted error is indistinguishable from an unwarranted error; unjustified true belief is lost: a lucky true guess is indistinguishable from a plain false belief. The taxonomy cannot say why a belief fails to be knowledge – false but justified vs true but unjustified vs both false and unjustified are all collapsed into mere Belief. Knowledge is thereby made a species of Belief K ⊂ B, which is counter-intuitive because knowledge is factive.

These are distinct from Gettier. The first is the Agrippa/Münchhausen regress/dogmatism/circularity problem for the J condition; the second is the loss of an intermediate epistemic category, the need for justified belief as distinct from both mere belief and knowledge. Unresolved nuance: whether the second problem is best phrased as “justification collapses into belief/knowledge” vs “belief heterogeneity”, but colleagues treat them as the same coarse-graining point.
reflection_text.4:
After round 0 the discussion converges on two linked difficulties for JTB when the only attitudinal categories allowed are Knowledge and Belief.

1. The justification condition cannot be independently grounded in a K/B ontology.
* If a justifier for p has to be an epistemic state, it is either a piece of Knowledge or a mere Belief.
* Identifying justification with Knowledge gives knowledge-of-knowledge / Meno’s regress: to know p you must know q that justifies p, to know q you must know r, etc. With only K and B this is an infinite regress of justifiers, or circular grounding K justified by K, or a dogmatic stop at beliefs taken as basic without epistemic support.
* Identifying justification with Belief makes justification non-factive and collapses justification into further belief: justified belief is belief justified by belief. Then you get the Agrippa/Münchhausen trilemma: infinite regress of beliefs justifying beliefs, circularity, or an arbitrary dogmatic foundation where some beliefs are taken as justified on fiat.
* In all cases justification cannot be a primitive independent mark; it either regresses, is circular, or is arbitrarily foundational. The J component of JTB has nowhere to live except as K or B.

2. Coarse-graining loss / heterogeneity of Belief and invisibility of justification as an independent epistemic dimension.
* On JTB the truth × justification matrix with belief held fixed is: J∧T = Knowledge; J∧¬T = justified false belief; ¬J∧T = unjustified true belief; ¬J∧¬T = unjustified false belief.
* With only K vs B, everything that is not J∧T∧B must be called Belief. Hence justified false belief, unjustified true belief, and unjustified false belief are all forced into the single undifferentiated Belief bin.
* Belief therefore becomes heterogeneous: it contains justified and unjustified beliefs, true and false beliefs. Justificatory status is lost outside the true case. A justified false belief is conflated with an unjustified false belief; an unjustified true belief is conflated with a justified false belief, etc. You can no longer say why a non-knowledge belief fails to be knowledge — false while justified vs true while unjustified vs both false and unjustified are indistinguishable.
* This also makes Knowledge a proper species of Belief, K⊂B, which is counter-intuitive given factivity, and makes justification epistemically invisible except when conjoined with truth in knowledge. That is the standard demand for an intermediate state, justified belief, between mere belief and knowledge.

Unresolved nuance: colleagues phrase the first problem as regress vs dogmatism vs circularity, and the second as collapse/heterogeneity vs K as species of B vs loss of warranted error and lucky true belief. Core agreement is that without a distinct justified-belief state JTB forces either an ungrounded justificatory chain or an epistemically blind K/B dichotomy. Gettier is explicitly bracketed.
reflection_text.6:
The question is to name the two classic pre-Gettier problems for JTB when the only available epistemic kinds are Knowledge and Belief.

Consensus from round 0 is essentially two interlocking failures.

1. The justification regress / Agrippa trilemma for the J condition.
Knowledge = Belief + Truth + Justification. With only K and B as states a justifier for p must itself be a K or a B. If it must be K, to know p you must know q that justifies p, know r that justifies q, etc. This yields Meno/Agrippa pressure: infinite regress of knowers/justifiers, circular justification where K justifies K, or dogmatic stopping at a belief taken as basic/unjustified. Colleagues 1,5,6,7,12 emphasize the classic infinite regress, and the only halts are arbitrary foundational beliefs accepted on fiat or circularity. Colleague 6/9 also notes the two readings: justification cashable in Knowledge → higher-order K Kp, K K Kp... or justification cashable in Belief → justification collapses into mere belief and can be licensed by false/unreliable beliefs. Either way J cannot be independently grounded in a K/B-only ontology.

2. Coarse-graining / loss of independent justification marking, i.e. heterogeneity and collapse of the Belief category.
On JTB the J×T matrix gives four cells: JT B = Knowledge; J F B = justified false belief; U T B = unjustified true belief; U F B = unjustified false belief. With only K vs B, the last three cells must all be labelled Belief.
Hence:
* Justified false belief is erased. A well-warranted error is indistinguishable from an unwarranted error; justification is invisible outside the true case.
* Unjustified true belief is erased. A lucky/accidental true belief is indistinguishable from a false belief; truth is invisible outside the justified case.
Belief therefore becomes the disjunctive class {justified false, unjustified true, unjustified false} and is epistemically heterogeneous. Knowledge is rendered a species of belief K⊂B, which is counter-intuitive given factivity. Colleagues 2,3,4,8,10,11 articulate this as the loss of distinct states Justified Belief and True Belief, and the inability to say why a non-knowledge belief fails to be knowledge.

These two points are often presented as regress/dogmatism vs collapse/heterogeneity. reflection_text.10:
The question is what goes wrong with JTB if the only epistemic kinds we are allowed are Knowledge and Belief, Gettier set aside.

Two distinct failures are repeatedly identified:

1. Justification cannot be grounded non-circularly without regress / dogmatism. Agrippa/Münchhausen trilemma.
If a belief p is to be justified, its justifier J1 must itself be an epistemic state, i.e. a piece of Knowledge or a mere Belief. If the justifier is required to be Knowledge, then knowing p requires knowing q that justifies p, requiring knowing r that justifies q, etc. That yields an infinite regress of ever higher order knowledge K p, K K p, … or circular grounding. If we try to stop, the stop must be a belief that is taken as justified without further epistemic support from K or B in the system: a basic / properly basic stopping point accepted on fiat. With only K and B that is dogmatic foundationalism. If justification is cashable in Belief alone, justification collapses into further belief, belief justifying belief, with no factive anchor, and knowledge becomes either unattainable or trivial. So J cannot be given a non-circular, non-regressive, non-dogmatic foundation on a K/B only ontology.

2. Epistemic coarse-graining / heterogeneity and loss of justification as an independent mark.
On JTB the J×T matrix with B held fixed has four cells:
J T B = Knowledge
J ¬T B = justified false belief
¬J T B = unjustified true belief
¬J ¬T B = unjustified false belief

With only Knowledge vs Belief, the last three cells must all be forced into the single undifferentiated Belief bin. Belief therefore becomes the disjunctive class {justified false belief, unjustified true belief, unjustified false belief}, i.e. heterogeneous. 
* Justified false belief is lost: a well-warranted error is indistinguishable from an unwarranted error; justificatory status is erased.
* Unjustified true belief is lost: a lucky true guess is indistinguishable from a false belief; truth-by-luck is erased.
Consequently you cannot say *why* a non-knowledge belief fails to be knowledge – it may fail for truth, for justification, or both, and the K/B dichotomy makes these failures invisible. Justification is only visible when conjoined with truth, i.e. only in Knowledge. The ordinary need for an intermediate state Justified Belief, distinct from both mere Belief and Knowledge, disappears.

These are often framed as the regress/closure problem and the collapse/heterogeneity problem. Knowledge is rendered a species of Belief K⊂B, which is counter-intuitive given factivity, and justification becomes epistemically invisible outside the true case. 3.text:
With a K/B only ontology JTB has nowhere to put the J condition as an independent mark.

1. Justification has no non-circular, non-regressive ground in K/B. 
On JTB K p = B p & T p & J p so a justifier for p must itself be an epistemic state. With only Knowledge and Belief available the justifier is either a piece of knowledge or a mere belief.

* If justification is cashed in Knowledge you need K J1 for p, K J2 for J1, etc. Knowledge requires knowledge of its own justification, so you get K p, K K p, K K K p … an infinite regress, or closure in a circle knowledge justified by knowledge. 
* If justification is cashed in Belief you get a chain B1 justifies B2 justifies B3 … with no terminus. The only halts are infinite regress, circular justification, or a dogmatic foundational stop at beliefs that are taken as basic and justified by fiat.

Hence the J condition cannot be given a non-arbitrary, non-circular foundation in a two-attitude ontology. Justification collapses either into higher-order knowledge or into mere belief, and the Agrippa/Münchhausen trilemma is forced.

2. The K/B dichotomy makes justification and truth epistemically invisible outside the J∧T∧B cell.
On the truth × justification matrix with belief held fixed

* J T B = Knowledge
* J F B = justified false belief
* U T B = unjustified true belief
* U F B = unjustified false belief

If the only labels you have are Knowledge and Belief, the last three cells must all be labelled Belief. Belief becomes the heterogeneous disjunctive class {justified false, unjustified true, unjustified false} and Knowledge is made a species of Belief, K ⊂ B.

That erases the two intermediate positions JTB is meant to track:

* Justified false belief is lost. A well warranted error is indistinguishable from an unwarranted error; the justificatory merit of the belief is erased in the Belief bin.
* Unjustified true belief is lost. A lucky true guess is indistinguishable from a plain false belief; the fact that the belief is true by accident is erased in the Belief bin.

In effect you can no longer say why a belief fails to be knowledge: false-but-justified, true-but-unjustified and false-and-unjustified are all collapsed into mere Belief. Justification ceases to be independently trackable except in the coincidence of truth and belief, i.e. only in knowledge. That is the coarse-graining / loss of a distinct justified-belief state between mere belief and knowledge, distinct from Gettier.

4.text:
With only K and B in the inventory the J component of JTB has no place to live independently of them, and the K/B dichotomy cannot carry the truth × justification structure that JTB requires.

1. Justification cannot be independently grounded in a K/B ontology. Justification of p must itself be an epistemic state, so it is either a piece of Knowledge or a mere Belief.

* If justification is cashable in Knowledge, to know p you must know q that justifies p, to know q you must know r that justifies q, etc. That is Meno’s regress / knowledge of knowledge. You get an infinite regress of justifiers, a circular grounding K justified by K, or you stop arbitrarily.
* If justification is cashable in Belief, justification is itself non-factive and collapses into further belief. Justified belief is belief justified by belief. That is the Agrippa/Münchhausen trilemma: an infinite regress of beliefs justifying beliefs, a circular chain, or a dogmatic stop at beliefs taken as basic on fiat.

In either reading the J condition is not a primitive third mark; it is either regressive/circular or dogmatic, and never non-circular, non-regressive and non-dogmatic.

2. Coarse graining / heterogeneity of Belief and the invisibility of justification as an independent dimension.

On JTB with belief held fixed the truth × justification matrix is

* J ∧ T ∧ B = Knowledge
* J ∧ ¬T ∧ B = justified false belief
* ¬J ∧ T ∧ B = unjustified true belief
* ¬J ∧ ¬T ∧ B = unjustified false belief

With only Knowledge vs Belief as kinds everything that is not J∧T∧B must be called Belief. Hence

* Justified false belief is conflated with unjustified false belief. A well-warranted error is epistemically indistinguishable from a mere error; the justificatory merit is lost outside the true case.
* Unjustified true belief is conflated with justified false belief and unjustified false belief. A lucky true guess is epistemically indistinguishable from a warranted falsehood; the fact that the belief is true by accident is lost.

Belief becomes the heterogeneous disjunctive class {justified false belief, unjustified true belief, unjustified false belief} and Knowledge becomes a proper species of Belief, K ⊂ B, which is counter-intuitive given factivity. You can no longer say why a non-knowledge belief fails to be knowledge — false while justified vs true while unjustified vs both false and unjustified are all the same “Belief”.

That is why JTB standardly demands an intermediate state, justified belief, between mere belief and knowledge. Gettier aside, a pure K/B taxonomy makes justification epistemically invisible except when conjoined with truth in knowledge.

1.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I think the regress pressure is real but it is a generic worry about grounding justification, not the specific damage you get from restricting the ontology to Knowledge and Belief only. With that restriction the JTB conjunction has nowhere to put the mixed cases, and that is what breaks the analysis.

On JTB K = J ∧ T ∧ B. Truth and justification are meant to be independently trackable. On a truth × justification matrix with belief held fixed you have four positions:

* J T = Knowledge
* J ¬T = justified false belief
* ¬J T = unjustified true belief
* ¬J ¬T = unjustified false belief

If the only states you are allowed to name are Knowledge and Belief, the last three cells have to be forced into a single undifferentiated Belief bin. That is not just a coarse-graining, it erases the two discriminations JTB is supposed to make.

First, justified false belief is lost. A subject can be fully justified by good evidence and still be false. On JTB that is not knowledge because truth fails, but it is epistemically good in the justification dimension. With only K vs B it must be called mere Belief, so a warranted error is conflated with an unwarranted error and the justificatory status disappears. You can no longer mark a belief as epistemically better because it is justified even though it is false.

Second, unjustified true belief is lost. A subject can believe p truly by luck, guess, coincidence, etc., without justification. On JTB that is not knowledge because justification fails, but it is true. With only K vs B it also has to be called mere Belief, so an accidentally true belief is conflated with a justified false belief and with an unjustified false belief. You can no longer mark the difference between a justified true belief which is knowledge and an unjustified true belief which is merely lucky.

In effect Belief becomes the heterogeneous disjunction {justified false, unjustified true, unjustified false} and justification and truth can only show up as difference-makers when they coincide, i.e. only in knowledge. That is the epistemic invisibility that forces the demand for a distinct justified-belief state between belief and knowledge, and it is the concrete taxonomic cost of a K/B-only ontology.

2.text:
With JTB K(p) = B(p) & T(p) & J(p) and only two kinds K and B to work with the J condition and the T/J matrix have nowhere independent to live.

1. Justification has no independent home and the Agrippa trilemma is forced on it. 
If a justifier for p is to be an epistemic state it is either a piece of Knowledge or a mere Belief. If it is Knowledge, to know p you need to know q which justifies p, and to know q you need to know r which justifies q, etc. That is a regress of justifiers, K→K→..., and in the limit either an infinite regress, a circular justification K justifies K, or a dogmatic stop. If it is mere Belief, justification is cashed out as belief that the belief is justified, i.e. J is reduced to B. The chain is then B1 justifies B2 justifies B3... with no stopping point, so the justification condition collapses into further belief and can only be halted by positing properly basic beliefs that are taken as justified by fiat. With a K/B only ontology JTB can therefore only be non-circular, non-regressive and non-dogmatic by stipulation, and justification never gets an independent non-primitive place to live.

2. The K/B dichotomy coarse-grains away the J×T distinctions that JTB is meant to mark. On the justification × truth matrix with belief held fixed there are four cells

* J T B = Knowledge
* J F B = justified false belief
* U T B = unjustified true belief
* U F B = unjustified false belief

With only Knowledge vs Belief available the last three cells are forced into the single undifferentiated Belief bin.

Hence Belief becomes heterogeneous. Justified false belief is conflated with unjustified false belief, so the justificatory merit of a false belief is lost; the taxonomy cannot mark that a belief is epistemically good in virtue of justification even though it is false.
Symmetrically unjustified true belief is conflated with justified false belief and unjustified false belief, so the luck/accident character of a true belief is lost; the taxonomy cannot mark that a belief fails to be knowledge because it is true by luck.

In effect justification is epistemically invisible except in the coincidence JT. Knowledge is made a species of belief K⊂B, and a non-knowledge belief can fail to be knowledge for three indistinguishable reasons - false but justified, true but unjustified, false and unjustified - because the K/B dichotomy has no intermediate state such as justified belief or true belief to express them. That is the classic pre-Gettier demand for a third state between mere belief and knowledge.

6.text:
With only the two attitude kinds *Knowledge* and *Belief* JTB cannot house the three independently variable dimensions it needs, Belief, Truth and Justification.

1. The Justification condition cannot be grounded in a K/B-only ontology.  
K = B & T & J. With K and B as the only states a justifier for p must itself be a K-state or a B-state.

* If justification is cashed out in Knowledge, to know p you must know q that justifies p, to know q you must know r that justifies q, etc. That is Meno/Agrippa pressure: an infinite regress of K K p, K K K p..., a circular justification K justified by K, or a dogmatic stop at a belief that is taken as justified without prior epistemic support.  
* If justification is cashed out in Belief, justification collapses into mere belief. Justified belief is then belief justified by belief, so a true belief can be ‘justified’ by a false or unreliable belief and the normative force of J disappears.  

In either reading J has no independent primitive place. The analysis is either viciously regressive/circular or terminates in ungrounded, properly basic beliefs accepted on fiat.

2. The K/B dichotomy coarse-grains away the justification × truth matrix.  
On JTB:

* J T B = Knowledge
* J F B = justified false belief
* U T B = unjustified true belief
* U F B = unjustified false belief

With only Knowledge vs Belief the last three cells must all be called Belief.

* Justified false belief is erased. A well warranted error is indistinguishable from an unwarranted error; the justificatory status of the belief is invisible outside the true case.
* Unjustified true belief is erased. A lucky/accidental true belief is indistinguishable from a false belief; truth is invisible outside the justified case.

Belief therefore becomes the heterogeneous disjunctive class {justified false, unjustified true, unjustified false} and Knowledge is rendered a species of belief, K ⊂ B. The taxonomy can no longer mark *why* a non-knowledge belief fails to be knowledge, i.e. whether it fails on T or on J. Justification is epistemically invisible as an independent mark of epistemic quality, which is the classic demand for an intermediate state such as Justified Belief distinct from both mere Belief and Knowledge.

10.text:
With only K and B as primitives J p = J p & T p & B p has nowhere to put J as an independent mark.

That gives two distinct failures.

1. Justification cannot be grounded non-circularly on a K/B ontology. Agrippa/Münchhausen.

If a belief p is to be justified its justifier J1 must itself be an epistemic state, i.e. K or B. If the justifier is required to be Knowledge then knowing p requires knowing q that justifies p, knowing r that justifies q, etc. That is an infinite regress of K p, K K p,... or a circular grounding in which knowledge is justified by knowledge. The only way to stop is to stop at a belief which is taken as justified without further epistemic support from K or B in the system. That is dogmatic foundationalism: basic beliefs accepted on fiat. If justification is cashed out in Belief alone justification collapses into belief justifying belief with no factive anchor, and knowledge becomes unattainable or trivial. Justification therefore cannot be given a non-circular, non-regressive, non-dogmatic foundation on a K/B only ontology.

2. Loss of justification as an independent, trackable epistemic mark and the heterogeneity of Belief.

On JTB with B held fixed the J×T matrix is:
J T B = Knowledge
J ¬T B = justified false belief
¬J T B = unjustified true belief
¬J ¬T B = unjustified false belief

With only the dichotomy Knowledge vs Belief the last three cells have to be forced into one undifferentiated Belief bin. Belief becomes the disjunctive class {justified false belief, unjustified true belief, unjustified false belief}.

* Justified false belief is lost: a well-warranted error is indistinguishable from an unwarranted error; the justificatory status of the belief is erased.
* Unjustified true belief is lost: a lucky true guess is indistinguishable from a false belief; truth-by-luck is erased.

Consequently you cannot say *why* a non-knowledge belief fails to be knowledge. It may fail for truth, for justification, or both, and the K/B dichotomy makes these failures invisible. Justification is only visible when conjoined with truth, i.e. only in Knowledge. The ordinary intermediate state Justified Belief, distinct from both mere Belief and Knowledge, disappears and K⊂B becomes counter-intuitive because knowledge is factive whereas belief is not.

That is the regress/closure problem and the collapse/heterogeneity coarse-graining problem.

7.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I’m with the point made by Colleagues 10, 2, 4 and 8 about the coarse-graining that a K/B only ontology forces on JTB, rather than treating Agrippa as the two distinct failures.

On JTB we need to track three independently relevant dimensions: Belief, Truth and Justification. With only two kinds available, Knowledge = J ∧ T ∧ B and Belief is then forced to be the remainder.

That makes the Belief class heterogeneous in a way that erases exactly the work JTB is meant to do.

1. Justified false belief is lost. J ∧ ¬T ∧ B is not Knowledge because Truth fails, but it is epistemically good on the Justification dimension. On a Knowledge vs Belief taxonomy it has to be called Belief, so a well-warranted error is collapsed with an unwarranted error and with an unjustified true belief. The justificatory status of the belief is invisible outside the true case.

2. Unjustified true belief is lost. T ∧ ¬J ∧ B is not Knowledge because Justification fails, but it is true. On a Knowledge vs Belief taxonomy it also has to be called Belief, so a lucky true guess is conflated with a justified false belief and with an unjustified false belief. The fact that the belief is true by accident is invisible, and the difference between a justified true belief which is Knowledge and an unjustified true belief which is merely Belief cannot be marked.

So Belief ends up being the disjunctive class {J F B, U T B, U F B} plus the K case when T and J coincide. Truth and Justification are no longer independently trackable epistemic properties; justification only shows up as a difference maker when conjoined with truth, i.e. only in Knowledge.

The regress/circularity pressure that Colleagues 1, 11, 12 and 6 flag is real, but it is the symptom of this collapse: once justification has nowhere except K or B to live in, cashing it out in K gives knowledge-of-knowledge and the familiar Agrippa chain, cashing it out in B makes justification just more belief. The underlying failure is that a K/B only inventory cannot host the intermediate states Justified Belief and True Belief that JTB needs to distinguish warranted error from unwarranted error and lucky truth from warranted truth. That is why we need a distinct justified-belief state between Belief and Knowledge, not just regress versus circularity as free-standing problems.

5.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: With a K/B-only ontology the justification clause of JTB has nowhere to live as an independent primitive.

1. The justification regress. To know that p on JTB you must be justified in believing p. If the justifier is itself an epistemic state it is either knowledge or mere belief. If it is knowledge you need a justifier for that knowledge, and for the justifier of that justifier, etc. That is the familiar Meno/Agrippa pressure: either the chain goes on forever or you have to stop it. With only Knowledge and Belief available the regress cannot be satisfied by a third, basic justified-but-not-known attitude, so the analysis is committed to an endless chain of justifiers or to an unexplained stopping point.

2. The coarse-graining / epistemic invisibility of justification and truth once JTB is forced into two kinds. On the analysis K = J ∧ T ∧ B the truth × justification matrix has four cells:

* J T B = Knowledge
* J F B = justified false belief
* U T B = unjustified true belief
* U F B = unjustified false belief

With only Knowledge and Belief as available states the last three cells must all be called Belief. The Belief category is therefore heterogeneous and justification/truth become trackable only in the conjunction that makes Knowledge.

* Justified false belief is lost. A belief can be fully warranted and still false. JTB says it is not knowledge because truth fails, but it is epistemically better than an unwarranted error. On a K/B dichotomy it has to be labelled mere Belief, so justified false belief is conflated with unjustified false belief and its justificatory status disappears.

* Unjustified true belief is lost. A belief can be true by luck, guess or coincidence without any warrant. JTB says it is not knowledge because justification fails, but it is true. On a K/B dichotomy it also has to be labelled mere Belief, so an accidentally true belief is conflated with a false belief and the fact that it is true is erased outside the knowledge case.

Hence justification can only show up as a difference-maker when conjoined with truth, i.e. only in Knowledge, and Belief becomes the disjunctive class {justified false belief, unjustified true belief, unjustified false belief}. That is the loss of a distinct justified-belief and true-belief space that JTB is meant to capture, and it is why the K/B dichotomy is normally said to make justification epistemically invisible. The regress pressure and the collapse/heterogeneity of Belief are the two distinct ways in which a purely Knowledge/Belief ontology makes JTB unable to do the work it is supposed to do, quite apart from Gettier.

8.text:
With JTB

K(p) := B(p) & T(p) & J(p)

the three conditions are meant to be independently trackable. If the only epistemic kinds you allow are K and B the J condition has no independent state in which to live and the four cells of the J×T matrix have to be squeezed into the K/B dichotomy. That gives the two pre-Gettier failures.

1. The justification condition has no non-circular, non-regressive, non-dogmatic grounding in a K/B ontology.
To know p you must be justified in believing p. The justifier itself must be an epistemic state, so it is either a piece of Knowledge or a mere Belief. If justification is cashed in Knowledge, to know p you must know q which justifies p, to know q you must know r which justifies q, etc. That is Meno/Agrippa: an infinite regress of justifiers, circularity K p justified by K p, or a dogmatic stop at beliefs that are taken as justified by fiat. If justification is cashed in mere Belief, justification collapses into further belief: B1 justifies B2 justifies B3... with no terminating, non-arbitrary ground. There is no room for an independently justified-but-not-known state to serve as a foundation, so J cannot be given a primitive, non-vicious account with only K and B.

2. The K/B dichotomy makes justification and truth epistemically invisible outside the true-justified case.
On the full matrix

* J T B = Knowledge
* J F B = justified false belief
* U T B = unjustified true belief
* U F B = unjustified false belief

If everything that is not J T B must be called Belief, Belief becomes the heterogeneous disjunction {J F B, U T B, U F B}. 

Hence justified false belief is lost: a warranted error is lumped with unwarranted error, so the justificatory merit of the belief disappears from the taxonomy. Symmetrically unjustified true belief is lost: a lucky/accidental true belief is lumped with false belief, so the truth merit disappears from the taxonomy. In particular K ⊂ B, knowledge is made a species of belief which is counter-intuitive because knowledge is factive, and the taxonomy can no longer say *why* a non-knowledge belief fails to be knowledge – failure can be falsity with justification, truth without justification, or both, and K vs B makes them indistinguishable.

That is the demand for an intermediate epistemic state, e.g. justified belief, distinct from both mere belief and knowledge.

9.text:
With JTB K = B ∧ T ∧ J and the ontology restricted to K and B the J condition has nowhere independent to live.

1.  Justification cannot be founded non-circularly, non-regressively and non-dogmatically on a K/B inventory.  
If a justifier for p has to be an epistemic state it is either a piece of Knowledge or a mere Belief.

* Knowledge of the justifier. * Belief of the justifier. To be justified in p you believe a justifier q, which itself needs a justifier r, etc. The chain is B1→B2→B3… and never terminates.

Justification is either infinitely deferred, circularly self-supporting, or arbitrarily grounded. The J condition cannot be given an independent, non-vicious foundation.

2.  Coarse-graining / heterogeneity of Belief and the invisibility of J and T outside K.

On JTB with B held fixed the J × T matrix is

* J T B = Knowledge
* J F B = justified false belief
* U T B = unjustified true belief
* U F B = unjustified false belief

With only Knowledge vs Belief as kinds the last three cells must all be forced into the single undifferentiated Belief bin. Belief becomes the disjunctive class
B = { J F B , U T B , U F B }.

Hence:
* Justified false belief is lost. A well-warranted error is epistemically good in J but not true, so on JTB it is not knowledge. On a K/B only taxonomy it has to be called mere Belief and is conflated with unjustified false belief. The justificatory status is erased.
* Unjustified true belief is lost. A lucky true guess is true but not justified, so on JTB it is not knowledge. On a K/B only taxonomy it also has to be called mere Belief and is conflated with justified false belief and unjustified false belief. The fact that the belief is true by accident is erased.

Justification and truth are therefore epistemically invisible except in the coincidence J∧T∧B. The Belief category is heterogeneous, and K entails B, K ⊂ B, so knowledge is rendered a species of belief which clashes with the factivity of knowledge vs the non-factivity of belief. The system can no longer say *why* a non-knowledge belief fails to be knowledge: failure of truth with justification, failure of justification with truth, or failure of both are all indistinguishable as mere Belief. That is the demand for an intermediate epistemic state such as justified belief / warranted belief / true belief distinct from knowledge.

PUBLIC RESPONSE: With only Knowledge and Belief as the inventory the JTB analysis cannot keep justification and truth as independently trackable marks, and that coarse-graining is what does the work in the two-state restriction.

On JTB the logical space with belief held fixed is the Truth × Justification matrix:

* J ∧ T ∧ B = Knowledge
* J ∧ ¬T ∧ B = justified false belief
* ¬J ∧ T ∧ B = unjustified true belief
* ¬J ∧ ¬T ∧ B = unjustified false belief

If the taxonomy is forced to Knowledge vs Belief, everything that is not J ∧ T ∧ B has to be called Belief. Justification and truth then stop being independently visible outside the Knowledge cell.

1. Justified false belief is lost in the Belief bin. A subject can be fully justified, e.g. by impeccable evidence, in believing p and p can still be false. JTB says that is not knowledge because Truth fails, but it is epistemically good in the Justification dimension. With only K/B the case must be labelled mere Belief and is thereby conflated with unjustified false belief and with unjustified true belief. The fact that the belief was justified is erased, so the system cannot mark a justified error as epistemically better than an unwarranted error.

2. Unjustified true belief is lost in the Belief bin. A subject can truly believe p by luck, guess or wishful thinking without any justification. JTB says that is not knowledge because Justification fails, but it is true. With only K/B the case also has to be labelled mere Belief and is thereby conflated with justified false belief and with unjustified false belief. The fact that the belief is true by accident is erased, so the system cannot mark a lucky true belief as epistemically worse than a justified true belief.

Hence Belief becomes a heterogeneous disjunctive class: { justified false belief, unjustified true belief, unjustified false belief }. Knowledge is rendered a species of Belief, K ⊂ B, and the ordinary factive contrast between knowing that p and merely believing that p disappears except in the external coincidence of truth and justification. That is why JTB needs an intermediate state, justified belief, which is neither Knowledge nor mere Belief, and why the two-state ontology makes justification epistemically invisible.

public_text.12:
With only Knowledge and Belief as the inventory the JTB analysis cannot keep justification and truth as independently trackable marks, and that coarse-graining is what does the work in the two-state restriction.

On JTB the logical space with belief held fixed is the Truth × Justification matrix:

* J ∧ T ∧ B = Knowledge
* J ∧ ¬T ∧ B = justified false belief
* ¬J ∧ T ∧ B = unjustified true belief
* ¬J ∧ ¬T ∧ B = unjustified false belief

If the taxonomy is forced to Knowledge vs Belief, everything that is not J ∧ T ∧ B has to be called Belief. Justification and truth then stop being independently visible outside the Knowledge cell.

1. Justified false belief is lost in the Belief bin. A subject can be fully justified, e.g. by impeccable evidence, in believing p and p can still be false. JTB says that is not knowledge because Truth fails, but it is epistemically good in the Justification dimension. With only K/B the case must be labelled mere Belief and is thereby conflated with unjustified false belief and with unjustified true belief. The fact that the belief was justified is erased, so the system cannot mark a justified error as epistemically better than an unwarranted error.

2. Unjustified true belief is lost in the Belief bin. A subject can truly believe p by luck, guess or wishful thinking without any justification. JTB says that is not knowledge because Justification fails, but it is true. With only K/B the case also has to be labelled mere Belief and is thereby conflated with justified false belief and with unjustified false belief. The fact that the belief is true by accident is erased, so the system cannot mark a lucky true belief as epistemically worse than a justified true belief.

Hence Belief becomes a heterogeneous disjunctive class: { justified false belief, unjustified true belief, unjustified false belief }. Knowledge is rendered a species of Belief, K ⊂ B, and the ordinary factive contrast between knowing that p and merely believing that p disappears except in the external coincidence of truth and justification. That is why JTB needs an intermediate state, justified belief, which is neither Knowledge nor mere Belief, and why the two-state ontology makes justification epistemically invisible.
