reflection_text.3:
The group is converging on two pre-Gettier failures of JTB when the ontology is restricted to only Knowledge and Belief, though there is some dispute over how to label/prioritise them.

1. Justification has no independent, non-vicious home in a K/B-only ontology; Agrippa/Münchhausen trilemma. 
If p is justified, the justifier J1 must itself be an epistemic state, so J1 is K or B. Cashing J in K gives K p → K q → K r... higher-order knowledge K p, K K p, K K K p, i.e. Meno/Agrippa regress, or circular grounding K justified by K. Cashing J in B gives B1 justifies B2 justifies B3... with no factive anchor; justification collapses into belief justifying belief. The only stops are infinite regress, circularity, or dogmatic foundationalism: basic beliefs taken as justified by fiat, or known without prior justification. With only K and B available there is no independently justified-but-not-known state to terminate the chain non-arbitrarily. This is the justification regress/closure problem.

2. Coarse-graining / heterogeneity and epistemic invisibility of justification/truth outside the JT coincidence.
On JTB K = J ∧ T ∧ B. With B held fixed the J×T matrix has four cells:
J T B = Knowledge
J ¬T B = justified false belief
¬J T B = unjustified true belief
¬J ¬T B = unjustified false belief
With only the dichotomy Knowledge vs Belief, the last three cells must all be forced into one undifferentiated Belief bin. Belief becomes the heterogeneous disjunction {justified false, unjustified true, unjustified false}, and K ⊂ B, making knowledge a species of belief which is counter-intuitive given factivity.

* Justified false belief is lost: a well-warranted error is indistinguishable from an unwarranted error; justificatory merit is erased outside the true case.
* Unjustified true belief is lost: a lucky/accidental true guess is indistinguishable from a false belief; truth-by-luck is erased.

Consequently you cannot say why a non-knowledge belief fails to be knowledge: failure can be falsity with justification, truth without justification, or both false and unjustified, all collapsed into mere Belief. Justification and truth are only independently trackable as difference-makers when they coincide in Knowledge. This is the demand for an intermediate state such as Justified Belief / True Belief distinct from both mere Belief and Knowledge.

Unresolved nuance: Colleague 1 and 7 stress that the regress pressure is really the symptom of the taxonomic collapse, and some colleagues present the coarse-graining as the concrete damage while others present the Agrippa trilemma as a free-standing problem. The core consensus remains the two problems above, distinct from Gettier, and that a K/B-only ontology makes justification epistemically invisible and forces an arbitrary foundation.
reflection_text.2:
The group consensus after round 1 remains the two pre-Gettier failures of JTB under a K/B-only ontology, with the current round reinforcing and nuancing both.

1. Justification grounding / Agrippa-Münchhausen trilemma. With only Knowledge and Belief as primitives, the J condition must be cashed out in K or B. If in K, to know p you need to know q that justifies p, to know q you need to know r that justifies q etc. → Meno/Agrippa regress K p, K K p, K K K p…, or circular self-justification K justified by K. If in B, justification collapses into belief justifying belief B1→B2→B3… with no factive anchor. The chain can only stop by infinite regress, circularity, or dogmatic foundationalism: basic beliefs taken as justified by fiat without independent epistemic support, or knowledge posited without prior justification. Justification therefore has no non-circular, non-regressive, non-dogmatic foundation and has no independent primitive place to live; J is either vacuous, higher-order knowledge, or mere further belief.

2. Coarse-graining / heterogeneity / epistemic invisibility of J and T. On JTB with belief held fixed the J×T matrix is J T B = Knowledge; J ¬T B = justified false belief; ¬J T B = unjustified true belief; ¬J ¬T B = unjustified false belief. With only the dichotomy Knowledge vs Belief, the three non-K cells must be forced into a single undifferentiated Belief bin. Belief becomes the heterogeneous disjunction {justified false belief, unjustified true belief, unjustified false belief} and K ⊂ B, making knowledge a species of belief, counter-intuitive given factivity.

* Justified false belief is lost: a warranted error is not knowledge because T fails, but is epistemically good in J. On K/B it is called mere Belief and is conflated with unjustified false belief; justificatory status is erased outside the true case.
* Unjustified true belief is lost: a lucky/accidental true belief is not knowledge because J fails, but is true. On K/B it is also called mere Belief and is conflated with justified false belief and unjustified false belief; truth-by-luck is erased.

Hence you can no longer say why a non-knowledge belief fails to be knowledge – failure of truth with justification, failure of justification with truth, or failure of both are all indistinguishable as Belief. Justification and truth are only independently trackable when conjoined, i.e. only in Knowledge. This is the classic demand for an intermediate state such as Justified Belief / True Belief distinct from mere Belief and Knowledge.

Colleagues largely treat these as two distinct failures; Colleague 7 stresses that the regress pressure is the symptom of the collapse, i.e. the underlying failure is the inability to host justified-belief and true-belief states, but the taxonomic loss and the Agrippa grounding problem are repeatedly reported together. No Gettier considerations are included, and no new distinct problems have been introduced in round 1.

¬J ¬T B = unjustified false belief

With only Knowledge vs Belief, the last three cells must be forced into one undifferentiated Belief bin. Belief becomes the heterogeneous disjunction {justified false belief, unjustified true belief, unjustified false belief} and K⊂B, making knowledge a species of belief, counter-intuitive given factivity.
* Justified false belief is lost: a well-warranted error is indistinguishable from an unwarranted error; justificatory status is erased outside the true case.
* Unjustified true belief is lost: a lucky true guess is indistinguishable from a false belief; truth-by-luck is erased.

Consequently you cannot say why a non-knowledge belief fails to be knowledge – failure may be truth, justification, or both – and justification/truth are only independently trackable when conjoined in Knowledge. The ordinary intermediate state Justified Belief, distinct from both mere Belief and Knowledge, disappears.

Unresolved nuance: how exactly regress and collapse interrelate – whether regress is the primary manifestation of the lack of an independent justification state, or a separate problem. The core demand remains for a distinct warrant/justification state and/or a factive attitude not a species of belief. No Gettier discussion.
reflection_text.8:
The JTB = Justified True Belief analysis with the ontology restricted to only Knowledge and Belief generates two interlocking pre-Gettier failures.

1. Justification has no independent primitive and cannot be grounded non-circularly, non-regressively, non-dogmatically on a K/B only ontology. 
K = B & T & J. A justifier for p must itself be an epistemic state, so it is either K or B.
* If justification is cashed in Knowledge: to know p you must know q that justifies p, to know q you must know r that justifies q, etc. → Meno/Agrippa regress K p, K K p, K K K p..., or circular grounding knowledge justified by knowledge, or dogmatic stop.
* If justification is cashed in Belief: justification collapses into belief justifying belief B1→B2→B3... with no terminating non-arbitrary ground. The only halts are infinite regress, circularity or foundational dogmatism: basic beliefs accepted on fiat.

Hence J cannot be given an independent non-vicious foundation; it is either regressive/circular or terminates in ungrounded properly basic beliefs. Some colleagues present this as Agrippa/Münchhausen trilemma, others note it is a symptom of the taxonomic collapse.

2. Taxonomic coarse-graining / heterogeneity / invisibility of justification and truth outside the J∧T∧B cell.
With belief held fixed the J×T matrix is:
J T B = Knowledge
J ¬T B = justified false belief
¬J T B = unjustified true belief
¬J ¬T B = unjustified false belief
With only K vs B, the last three cells are forced into a single undifferentiated Belief bin.

Belief becomes the heterogeneous disjunction {justified false belief, unjustified true belief, unjustified false belief} and K ⊂ B, making knowledge a species of belief contrary to factivity.

* Justified false belief is lost: a warranted error is indistinguishable from an unwarranted error; justificatory merit is invisible outside the true case.
* Unjustified true belief is lost: a lucky/accidental true belief is indistinguishable from false belief; truth-by-luck is invisible outside the justified case.

Thus the system cannot say why a non-knowledge belief fails to be knowledge – failure can be falsity with justification, truth without justification, or both – and justification/truth are only trackable together in the coincident case of Knowledge. This is the classic demand for an intermediate state such as justified belief / true belief distinct from both mere belief and knowledge.

Disagreement nuance in round 1: Colleague 1 and Colleague 7 stress that the regress pressure is generic and the specific damage of the K/B restriction is the erasure of the mixed J×T cells. Others frame regress/closure and collapse/heterogeneity as two distinct problems. Consensus remains that both the grounding regress/dogmatism problem and the collapse/heterogeneity invisibility problem are the two pre-Gettier costs of a pure Knowledge/Belief ontology.

With a K/B only inventory JTB has no room for J and T as independently trackable marks.

K = B ∧ T ∧ J. With B held fixed the J×T space is

* J T B = Knowledge

* ¬J T B = unjustified true belief
* ¬J ¬T B = unjustified false belief

* $\lnot J \lnot T B$ = unjustified false belief

1. Justification has no non-vicious grounding on a K/B ontology.  
A justifier for p must itself be an epistemic state, so it is either K or B.
* If justification is cashed in Knowledge, to know p you must know q that justifies p, to know q you must know r that justifies q, etc. That is Meno/Agrippa regress K p, K K p, K K K p…, closed only by circular knowledge-justified-by-knowledge or by a dogmatic stop.
* If justification is cashed in Belief, justification collapses into B1 justifies B2 justifies B3… with no terminating non-arbitrary ground.

Hence on a K/B only inventory J is either infinitely regressive, circularly self-supporting, or dogmatically foundational. Justification cannot be given an independent, non-circular, non-regressive, non-dogmatic foundation; it is either vacuous or ungrounded.

2. Taxonomic coarse-graining / epistemic invisibility of J and T outside the JT coincidence.  
With B held fixed the J × T matrix is

* J T B = Knowledge
* J ¬T B = justified false belief
* ¬J T B = unjustified true belief
* ¬J ¬T B = unjustified false belief

With only Knowledge vs Belief the last three cells must be forced into one undifferentiated Belief bin. Belief becomes the heterogeneous disjunction {justified false belief, unjustified true belief, unjustified false belief} and K ⊂ B.

* Justified false belief is lost. A warranted error is not knowledge because truth fails, but it is epistemically good in justification. On K/B it must be called mere Belief and is conflated with unwarranted error; justificatory merit is invisible outside the true case.
* Unjustified true belief is lost. A lucky/accidental true belief is not knowledge because justification fails, but it is true. On K/B it must also be called mere Belief and is conflated with justified false belief and unjustified false belief; truth-by-luck is invisible outside the justified case.

Justification and truth are therefore only trackable as difference-makers when they coincide in Knowledge. The system can no longer say why a non-knowledge belief fails to be knowledge - failure for falsity with justification, for truth without justification, or for both are all indistinguishable as mere Belief. This is the classic demand for an intermediate state such as Justified Belief / True Belief distinct from both mere Belief and Knowledge.

9.text:
With JTB K = B ∧ T ∧ J and B held fixed the J × T matrix is

* J T B = Knowledge
* J ¬T B = justified false belief
* ¬J T B = unjustified true belief
* ¬J ¬T B = unjustified false belief

On a Knowledge / Belief only inventory everything that is not J T B must be called Belief. Justification then has no independent primitive place to live.

1. Justification cannot be grounded non-circularly, non-regressively and non-dogmatically on K/B.

A justifier for p must itself be an epistemic state, so it is K or B.

* Cashing J in Knowledge: to know p you must know q that justifies p, to know q you must know r that justifies q, etc. K p → K K p → K K K p … i.e. Meno/Agrippa regress of higher-order knowledge, or circular grounding K justified by K, or an arbitrary stop.
* Cashing J in Belief: justification is B1 justifies B2 justifies B3 … with no factive anchor. The chain terminates only by fiat at properly basic beliefs taken as justified simpliciter.

J therefore has no independent non-vicious foundation on a K/B ontology; it is either infinitely deferred, circularly self-supporting, or dogmatically stopped. That is the Agrippa/Münchhausen pressure that is forced once justification has nowhere except K or B to live.

2. The K/B dichotomy coarse-grains away the independent J and T marks and makes Belief heterogeneous.

With only Knowledge vs Belief the three remaining cells are forced into one undifferentiated Belief bin:

Belief = { J ¬T B , ¬J T B , ¬J ¬T B }.

* Justified false belief is erased. A well warranted error is not Knowledge because T fails, but it is epistemically good in J. On K/B it must be called mere Belief and is conflated with unjustified false belief, so justificatory merit disappears outside the true case.
* Unjustified true belief is erased. A lucky true guess is not Knowledge because J fails, but it is true. On K/B it must also be called mere Belief and is conflated with justified false belief and unjustified false belief, so truth-by-luck disappears outside the justified case.

Justification and truth are therefore epistemically invisible except in their coincidence J∧T∧B. Knowledge becomes a species of Belief K ⊂ B, and a non-knowledge belief can fail to be knowledge for three indistinguishable reasons — false but justified, true but unjustified, false and unjustified — because the taxonomy has no intermediate state such as justified belief or true belief between mere Belief and Knowledge. That is the loss of independent epistemic granularity, the concrete taxonomic cost of the two-state restriction.

PUBLIC RESPONSE: I think the specific damage you get from a Knowledge/Belief-only ontology is best seen as a taxonomic collapse rather than as a free-standing grounding puzzle.

On JTB K = B ∧ J ∧ T and with belief held fixed we need the Truth × Justification matrix:

* J T B = Knowledge
* J ¬T B = justified false belief
* ¬J T B = unjustified true belief
* ¬J ¬T B = unjustified false belief

If the only labels you are allowed to use are Knowledge vs Belief, everything that is not J T B has to be forced into a single undifferentiated Belief bin. Belief then becomes the heterogeneous disjunction {justified false, unjustified true, unjustified false}. Justification and truth are only visible as difference-makers when they coincide, i.e. only in Knowledge.

That gives two concrete, ontology-relative losses.

First, justified false belief is lost in the Belief bin. A subject can be fully justified by good evidence and still be false. JTB says that is not knowledge because truth fails, but it is epistemically good in the justification dimension. On a K/B dichotomy it must be called mere Belief and is thereby conflated with unjustified false belief and with unjustified true belief. The justificatory merit of a warranted error disappears; you can no longer mark a belief as epistemically better because it is justified even though it is false.

Second, unjustified true belief is lost in the Belief bin. A subject can truly believe p by luck, guess or coincidence without justification. JTB says that is not knowledge because justification fails, but it is true. On a K/B dichotomy it also has to be called mere Belief and is thereby conflated with justified false belief and with unjustified false belief. The fact that the belief is true by accident is erased; you can no longer mark the difference between a justified true belief which is knowledge and an unjustified true belief which is merely lucky.

Hence Belief becomes epistemically invisible as an intermediate class and Knowledge becomes a proper species of belief K ⊂ B. The system can no longer say why a non-knowledge belief fails to be knowledge — failure of truth with justification, failure of justification with truth, or failure of both — are all indistinguishable as “mere Belief.”

That is the demand for a distinct justified-belief state between mere belief and knowledge, and it is why with only K and B available justification and truth cease to be independently trackable marks outside the coincident J∧T case. The Agrippa pressure many of us note is the symptom of this collapse: once justification has nowhere except K or B to live, cashing it out in K gives knowledge-of-knowledge and cashing it out in B makes justification just more belief.

1. Justification has no non-vicious grounding on a K/B ontology.  
A justifier for p must itself be an epistemic state, so it is either K or B.

* If justification is cashed in Belief, justification collapses into B1 justifies B2 justifies B3… with no terminating non-arbitrary ground.

With B held fixed the J × T matrix is

* J T B = Knowledge
* J ¬T B = justified false belief
* ¬J T B = unjustified true belief
* ¬J ¬T B = unjustified false belief

With only Knowledge vs Belief the last three cells must be forced into one undifferentiated Belief bin. Belief becomes the heterogeneous disjunction {justified false belief, unjustified true belief, unjustified false belief} and K ⊂ B.

* Justified false belief is lost. A warranted error is not knowledge because truth fails, but it is epistemically good in justification. On K/B it must be called mere Belief and is conflated with unwarranted error; justificatory merit is invisible outside the true case.
* Unjustified true belief is lost. A lucky/accidental true belief is not knowledge because justification fails, but it is true. On K/B it must also be called mere Belief and is conflated with justified false belief and unjustified false belief; truth-by-luck is invisible outside the justified case.

The system can no longer say why a non-knowledge belief fails to be knowledge - failure for falsity with justification, for truth without justification, or for both are all indistinguishable as mere Belief. I think the specific damage you get from a Knowledge/Belief-only ontology is best seen as a taxonomic collapse rather than as a free-standing grounding puzzle.

On JTB K = B ∧ J ∧ T and with belief held fixed we need the Truth × Justification matrix:

* J T B = Knowledge
* J ¬T B = justified false belief
* ¬J T B = unjustified true belief
* ¬J ¬T B = unjustified false belief

If the only labels you are allowed to use are Knowledge vs Belief, everything that is not J T B has to be forced into a single undifferentiated Belief bin. Belief then becomes the heterogeneous disjunction {justified false, unjustified true, unjustified false}. Justification and truth are only visible as difference-makers when they coincide, i.e. only in Knowledge.

That gives two concrete, ontology-relative losses.

First, justified false belief is lost in the Belief bin. A subject can be fully justified by good evidence and still be false. JTB says that is not knowledge because truth fails, but it is epistemically good in the justification dimension. On a K/B dichotomy it must be called mere Belief and is thereby conflated with unjustified false belief and with unjustified true belief. The justificatory merit of a warranted error disappears; you can no longer mark a belief as epistemically better because it is justified even though it is false.

Second, unjustified true belief is lost in the Belief bin. A subject can truly believe p by luck, guess or coincidence without justification. JTB says that is not knowledge because justification fails, but it is true. On a K/B dichotomy it also has to be called mere Belief and is thereby conflated with justified false belief and with unjustified false belief. The fact that the belief is true by accident is erased; you can no longer mark the difference between a justified true belief which is knowledge and an unjustified true belief which is merely lucky.

Hence Belief becomes epistemically invisible as an intermediate class and Knowledge becomes a proper species of belief K ⊂ B. The system can no longer say why a non-knowledge belief fails to be knowledge — failure of truth with justification, failure of justification with truth, or failure of both — are all indistinguishable as “mere Belief.”

That is the demand for a distinct justified-belief state between mere belief and knowledge, and it is why with only K and B available justification and truth cease to be independently trackable marks outside the coincident J∧T case. The Agrippa pressure many of us note is the symptom of this collapse: once justification has nowhere except K or B to live, cashing it out in K gives knowledge-of-knowledge and cashing it out in B makes justification just more belief.

I think we can get a clearer picture by separating the grounding worry from the taxonomic worry, and keeping the Agrippa trilemma together as one pressure.

Colleagues 11 and 6 are right that on a K/B only ontology the J condition has no independent primitive place to live. With K = B & T & J a justifier for p must itself be an epistemic state, so it is either Knowledge or mere Belief. If it is Knowledge you need a justifier for the justifier, and so on. That is the familiar Meno/Agrippa pressure: a chain of justifiers K p → K K p → K K K p … or B1 → B2 → B3 … with no non-arbitrary terminus. Circularity and dogmatic stopping are just the two ways the chain is closed once you refuse infinite ascent; they are variants of the same grounding problem rather than two free-standing failures. The point is that justification cannot be given a non-circular, non-regressive, non-dogmatic foundation when the only attitudes you can name are Knowledge and Belief.

That grounding pressure is real, but it is distinct from the second cost that the K/B restriction forces on the J×T structure itself. That is the point made very clearly by Colleagues 1, 10, 12, 2, 3, 4, 8 and 9: with belief held fixed JTB wants the four cells

* J T B = Knowledge
* J ¬T B = justified false belief
* ¬J T B = unjustified true belief
* ¬J ¬T B = unjustified false belief

If the taxonomy is forced to Knowledge vs Belief, everything that is not J∧T∧B must be called Belief. Belief then becomes the heterogeneous disjunction {justified false, unjustified true, unjustified false}. Justification and truth are only independently visible when they coincide in Knowledge.

First, justified false belief is lost. A belief can be fully warranted by good evidence and still be false. JTB says that is not knowledge because truth fails, but it is epistemically good in the justification dimension. On a K/B dichotomy it has to be labelled mere Belief and is conflated with unwarranted error. The justificatory merit disappears outside the true case.

Second, unjustified true belief is lost. A belief can be true by luck, guess or coincidence without warrant. JTB says that is not knowledge because justification fails, but it is true. On a K/B dichotomy it also has to be labelled mere Belief and is conflated with justified false belief and with unjustified false belief. The fact that the belief is true by accident is erased outside Knowledge.

In effect Belief becomes epistemically invisible as a coarse-grained bin, and Knowledge becomes a species of Belief K ⊂ B. We can no longer say *why* a non-knowledge belief fails to be knowledge – false but justified, true but unjustified, and false and unjustified are all indistinguishable as mere Belief. reflection_text.4:
The discussion has stabilised on two pre-Gettier difficulties for JTB when the epistemic inventory is restricted to Knowledge and Belief only, and Gettier is explicitly bracketed.

1. Justification has no independent, non-vicious home on a K/B ontology; the Agrippa/Münchhausen grounding pressure.
* On JTB K p = B p & T p & J p. A justifier for p must itself be an epistemic state, i.e. K or B.
* Cashing J in Knowledge gives Meno/Agrippa pressure: to know p you must know q that justifies p, to know q you must know r… K p, K K p, K K K p… infinite regress of higher-order knowledge, or circular grounding K justified by K, or an arbitrary dogmatic stop at a belief known without prior justification.
* Cashing J in Belief makes justification non-factive and collapses into belief-justifying-belief: B1 justifies B2 justifies B3… with no terminating non-arbitrary ground and no factive anchor. The only halts are infinite regress, circularity or dogmatic foundationalism: basic beliefs taken as justified by fiat.
* Hence J is either regressive/circular, vacuous, or dogmatically foundational. Justification cannot be given a non-circular, non-regressive, non-dogmatic foundation on a K/B inventory; it has no primitive location distinct from K and B. Colleagues variously phrase this as Meno’s regress, closure, Agrippa trilemma, knowledge-of-knowledge.

2. Coarse-graining / heterogeneity of Belief and epistemic invisibility of justification/truth outside Knowledge; loss of the J × T matrix.
* With B held fixed JTB wants: J T B = Knowledge; J ¬T B = justified false belief; ¬J T B = unjustified true belief; ¬J ¬T B = unjustified false belief.
* With only Knowledge vs Belief the last three cells must be forced into a single undifferentiated Belief bin. Belief becomes the heterogeneous disjunction {justified false belief, unjustified true belief, unjustified false belief} and Knowledge becomes a proper species of Belief K ⊂ B, counter to factivity.
* Justified false belief is lost: a warranted error is not knowledge because T fails but is epistemically good in J. On K/B it must be called mere Belief and is conflated with unjustified false belief and unjustified true belief; justificatory merit is invisible outside the true case.
* Unjustified true belief is lost: a lucky/accidental true belief is not knowledge because J fails but is true. On K/B it is also called mere Belief and is conflated with justified false and unjustified false belief; truth-by-luck is invisible outside the justified case.
* Justification and truth are therefore only independently trackable when conjoined in Knowledge. The taxonomy can no longer say why a non-knowledge belief fails to be knowledge: failure of truth with justification, failure of justification with truth, or failure of both are indistinguishable as mere Belief. This forces the demand for an intermediate state such as Justified Belief / True Belief between mere Belief and Knowledge.

Unresolved nuance is mainly terminological/ordering. Some colleagues foreground the regress/closure grounding worry as the core problem and treat coarse-graining as its expression; others foreground coarse-graining/heterogeneity/loss of warranted error and lucky true belief as the concrete taxonomic cost of the K/B restriction, with Agrippa pressure as the symptom of the collapse. Core shared view remains that without a distinct justified-belief state JTB forces either an ungrounded justificatory chain and a K/B dichotomy that makes justification epistemically invisible, and this is distinct from Gettier.
reflection_text.3:
The group remains converged on two pre-Gettier failures of JTB under a strict Knowledge/Belief only ontology, though there is ongoing dispute about how to weight and label them.

1. Justification has no independent, non-vicious home in a K/B-only ontology; Agrippa/Münchhausen grounding pressure.
If p is justified its justifier J1 must itself be an epistemic state, so J1 is K or B. Cashing J in K gives K p → K q → K r... i.e. Meno/Agrippa regress K p, K K p, K K K p..., or circular grounding K justified by K, or an arbitrary dogmatic stop. Cashing J in B gives B1 justifies B2 justifies B3... with no factive anchor; justification collapses into belief justifying belief. The only halts are infinite regress, circularity or dogmatic foundationalism: basic beliefs taken as justified by fiat, or known without prior justification. With only K and B there is no independently justified-but-not-known state to terminate the chain non-arbitrarily. Colleagues 5, 11, 6, 9 treat infinite regress, circularity and dogmatism as variants of the same grounding trilemma; colleagues 1, 7, 12 argue the regress is the symptom of the taxonomic collapse.

2. Coarse-graining / heterogeneity and epistemic invisibility of justification/truth outside the JT coincidence.
On JTB K = J ∧ T ∧ B. With B held fixed the J×T matrix has four cells:
J T B = Knowledge
J ¬T B = justified false belief
¬J T B = unjustified true belief
¬J ¬T B = unjustified false belief
With only Knowledge vs Belief the last three cells are forced into one undifferentiated Belief bin. Belief becomes the heterogeneous disjunction {justified false, unjustified true, unjustified false} and K ⊂ B, making knowledge a species of belief which is counter-intuitive given factivity.
* Justified false belief is erased: a well-warranted error is indistinguishable from an unwarranted error; justificatory merit is invisible outside the true case.
* Unjustified true belief is erased: a lucky/accidental true guess is indistinguishable from a false belief; truth-by-luck is invisible.
Consequently you cannot say why a non-knowledge belief fails to be knowledge: failure can be falsity with justification, truth without justification, or both false and unjustified, all collapsed into mere Belief. Justification and truth are only independently trackable as difference-makers when they coincide in Knowledge. This is the demand for an intermediate state such as Justified Belief / True Belief distinct from both mere Belief and Knowledge.

Consensus: the four-cell matrix is the shared formal picture; the specific taxonomic cost is the loss of justified false belief and unjustified true belief and the heterogeneity of Belief. Unresolved nuance: whether the Agrippa grounding pressure counts as a free-standing second problem or as the generic symptom of the taxonomic collapse once justification has nowhere except K or B to live. Colleagues 1,7 stress taxonomic collapse as the specific damage of the K/B restriction, with regress as symptom; colleagues 10,11,2,3,4,6,8,9 present both grounding and coarse-graining as two distinct pre-Gettier failures. No disagreement on the content of the two losses.
reflection_text.2:
The group consensus after round 2 remains two pre-Gettier failures of JTB under a K/B-only ontology, now with a clearer articulation of their relationship and emphasis.

1. Justification grounding / Agrippa-Münchhausen trilemma on a K/B inventory. With only Knowledge and Belief as primitives the J condition must be cashed out in K or B. 
* If in K: to know p you need to know q that justifies p, to know q you need to know r that justifies q… → Meno/Agrippa regress K p, K K p, K K K p…, or circular self-justification K justified by K.
* If in B: justification collapses into belief justifying belief B1→B2→B3… with no factive anchor.
The chain can only stop by infinite regress, circularity, or dogmatic foundationalism: basic beliefs taken as justified by fiat, or knowledge posited without prior justification. Justification therefore has no non-circular, non-regressive, non-dogmatic foundation and has no independent primitive place to live; J is either vacuous, higher-order knowledge, or mere further belief.

Colleagues 1,7,12, and notably 7, now stress that this regress pressure is the symptom of the collapse, i.e. the underlying failure is the inability to host justified-belief and true-belief states. Most still report it as a distinct grounding problem, separate from but linked to the taxonomic loss.

2. Coarse-graining / heterogeneity / epistemic invisibility of J and T. On JTB with belief held fixed the J×T matrix is J T B = Knowledge; J ¬T B = justified false belief; ¬J T B = unjustified true belief; ¬J ¬T B = unjustified false belief. With only Knowledge vs Belief the three non-K cells must be forced into a single undifferentiated Belief bin. Belief becomes the heterogeneous disjunction {justified false belief, unjustified true belief, unjustified false belief} and K ⊂ B, making knowledge a species of belief, counter-intuitive given factivity.
* Justified false belief is lost: a warranted error is not knowledge because T fails, but is epistemically good in J. On K/B it is called mere Belief and is conflated with unjustified false belief; justificatory status is erased outside the true case.
* Unjustified true belief is lost: a lucky/accidental true belief is not knowledge because J fails, but is true. On K/B it is also called mere Belief and is conflated with justified false belief and unjustified false belief; truth-by-luck is erased.

Hence you can no longer say why a non-knowledge belief fails to be knowledge – failure of truth with justification, failure of justification with truth, or failure of both are all indistinguishable as Belief. Justification and truth are only independently trackable when conjoined, i.e. only in Knowledge. This is the classic demand for an intermediate state such as Justified Belief / True Belief distinct from mere Belief and Knowledge.

The discussion in round 2 sharpens the taxonomy loss as the specific damage of the two-state restriction, while retaining the Agrippa grounding pressure as the formal expression of J having nowhere independent to live. No Gettier considerations are included, and no new distinct problems have been introduced. The remaining tension is whether the regress is a free-standing failure or the symptom of the coarse-graining; for practical purposes the two are reported together as the two pre-Gettier problems.

reflection_text.10:
The question is what goes wrong with JTB if the only epistemic kinds allowed are Knowledge and Belief, Gettier set aside. With B held fixed the J×T matrix has four cells:
J T B = Knowledge
J ¬T B = justified false belief
¬J T B = unjustified true belief
¬J ¬T B = unjustified false belief

With only Knowledge vs Belief, the last three cells must be forced into one undifferentiated Belief bin. Belief becomes the heterogeneous disjunction {justified false belief, unjustified true belief, unjustified false belief} and K⊂B, making knowledge a species of belief, counter-intuitive given factivity.
* Justified false belief is lost: a well-warranted error is indistinguishable from an unwarranted error; justificatory merit is invisible outside the true case.
* Unjustified true belief is lost: a lucky true guess is indistinguishable from a false belief; truth-by-luck is erased.

Consequently you cannot say why a non-knowledge belief fails to be knowledge – failure may be truth, justification, or both – and justification/truth are only independently trackable when conjoined in Knowledge. 4.text:
With JTB K = B ∧ T ∧ J and B held fixed JTB wants the J × T matrix

* J T B = Knowledge
* J ¬T B = justified false belief
* ¬J T B = unjustified true belief
* ¬J ¬T B = unjustified false belief

On a strict Knowledge vs Belief inventory the last three cells have to be forced into one undifferentiated Belief bin. That is the pre-Gettier damage of the two-state restriction.

1. Justification has no independent, non-vicious home on a K/B ontology. The Agrippa/Münchhausen grounding pressure.

A justifier for p must itself be an epistemic state, i.e. K or B.

* Cashed in Knowledge: to know p you must know q that justifies p, to know q you must know r that justifies q, etc. K p → K K p → K K K p… Meno regress of higher-order knowledge, or closure by circular knowledge-justified-by-knowledge, or an arbitrary dogmatic stop at a belief known without prior justification.
* Cashed in Belief: justification collapses into B1 justifies B2 justifies B3… belief-justifying-belief with no factive anchor.

Hence on K/B J is either infinitely regressive, circularly self-supporting, or dogmatically foundational. Justification cannot be given a non-circular, non-regressive, non-dogmatic foundation and has no primitive location distinct from K and B.

2. Coarse-graining / epistemic invisibility of J and T outside the J∧T coincidence; heterogeneity of Belief.

With only Knowledge vs Belief Belief becomes the heterogeneous disjunction
Belief = { J ¬T B , ¬J T B , ¬J ¬T B } and K ⊂ B.

* Justified false belief is lost. A warranted error is not knowledge because T fails but is epistemically good in J. On K/B it must be called mere Belief and is conflated with unjustified false belief and with unjustified true belief. Justificatory merit is invisible outside the true case.
* Unjustified true belief is lost. A lucky/accidental true belief is not knowledge because J fails but is true. On K/B it also must be called mere Belief and is conflated with justified false belief and unjustified false belief. Truth-by-luck is invisible outside the justified case.

Justification and truth are therefore only difference-makers when conjoined in Knowledge. The taxonomy can no longer say why a non-knowledge belief fails to be knowledge — failure of truth with justification, failure of justification with truth, or failure of both — are all indistinguishable as mere Belief. That is the demand for an intermediate state such as Justified Belief / True Belief between mere Belief and Knowledge, distinct from Gettier.

1.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I think the framing Colleagues 1, 12 and 7 pull out is the right way to read the question, once we separate a generic grounding worry from the damage that is specific to a Knowledge/Belief only inventory.

Yes, JTB needs justification to be grounded non-circularly and non-dogmatically, and on a bare K/B inventory that grounding pressure is visible. A justifier for p has to be an epistemic state, so it is K or B, and cashing J in K gives the familiar Meno/Agrippa ascent and cashing J in B makes justification just belief-justifying-belief. That pressure is real, but it is the generic Agrippa problem for any JTB view. It is not the specific, ontology-relative damage you get from restricting the labels to Knowledge vs Belief.

With B held fixed JTB is meant to track the J × T matrix:
* J T B = Knowledge
* J ¬T B = justified false belief
* ¬J T B = unjustified true belief
* ¬J ¬T B = unjustified false belief

If the only names allowed are Knowledge and Belief, the three non-K cells are forced into one undifferentiated Belief bin. Belief becomes the heterogeneous disjunction {justified false, unjustified true, unjustified false} and K ⊂ B. Justification and truth are then only difference-makers when they coincide.

That gives two concrete, ontology-relative losses, and those are the two pre-Gettier problems the restriction creates.

First, justified false belief is erased. A belief can be fully warranted by good evidence and still be false. JTB says it is not knowledge because truth fails, but it is epistemically good on the justification dimension. On a K/B dichotomy it must be called mere Belief and is conflated with unjustified false belief and with unjustified true belief. The justificatory merit of a warranted error disappears; you can no longer mark a belief as better because it is justified even though false.

Second, unjustified true belief is erased. A belief can be true by luck, guess or coincidence without warrant. JTB says it is not knowledge because justification fails, but it is true. On a K/B dichotomy it also has to be called mere Belief and is conflated with justified false belief and with unjustified false belief. The fact that the belief is true by accident is erased; you can no longer mark the difference between a justified true belief which is knowledge and an unjustified true belief which is merely lucky.

So the system can no longer say why a non-knowledge belief fails to be knowledge: failure of truth with justification, failure of justification with truth, and failure of both are all indistinguishable as “mere Belief.” That is the demand for an intermediate state between mere Belief and Knowledge, and the reason justification and truth cease to be independently trackable marks outside the J∧T∧B coincidence. The Agrippa pressure many of us note is the symptom of this collapse, not two free-standing failures distinct from the coarse-graining itself.

I think the specific damage you get from a Knowledge/Belief only ontology is best seen as a taxonomic collapse rather than as a free-standing grounding puzzle, and that is why the two pre-Gettier failures are visible in the J×T matrix with B held fixed.

JTB wants three independently variable marks: B, T and J. With B held fixed we should be able to track

* J T B = Knowledge
* J ¬T B = justified false belief
* ¬J T B = unjustified true belief
* ¬J ¬T B = unjustified false belief

If the only labels you are allowed to use are Knowledge vs Belief, everything that is not J T B has to be forced into a single undifferentiated Belief bin. Belief then becomes the heterogeneous disjunction {J ¬T B, ¬J T B, ¬J ¬T B} and K ⊂ B. Justification and truth are only difference-makers when they coincide, i.e. only in Knowledge.

That gives two concrete, ontology-relative losses which are the operational content of the K/B restriction.

First, justified false belief is lost in the Belief bin. A subject can be fully justified by good evidence and still be false. JTB says that is not knowledge because truth fails, but it is epistemically good in the justification dimension. On a K/B dichotomy it must be called mere Belief and is conflated with unjustified false belief and with unjustified true belief. The justificatory merit of a warranted error disappears; you can no longer mark a belief as better because it is justified even though it is false.

Second, unjustified true belief is lost in the Belief bin. A subject can truly believe p by luck, guess or coincidence without justification. JTB says that is not knowledge because justification fails, but it is true. On a K/B dichotomy it also has to be called mere Belief and is conflated with justified false belief and with unjustified false belief. The fact that the belief is true by accident is erased; you can no longer distinguish a justified true belief which is knowledge from an unjustified true belief which is merely lucky.

Hence Belief becomes epistemically invisible as an intermediate class and we can no longer say why a non-knowledge belief fails to be knowledge – failure of truth with justification, failure of justification with truth, or failure of both – are all indistinguishable as “mere Belief”.

Once justification has nowhere except K or B to live, cashing it out in K gives knowledge-of-knowledge and cashing it out in B makes justification just more belief. That grounding worry is generic to justification, not distinctive to the two-state restriction. The distinctive damage of the K/B restriction is the coarse-graining that erases justified false belief and unjustified true belief, i.e. the loss of an independent justified-belief / true-belief state between mere Belief and Knowledge.

PRIVATE REFLECTION: The JTB = Justified True Belief analysis with an ontology restricted to only Knowledge and Belief generates two interlocking pre-Gettier costs, now repeatedly articulated as justification grounding / Agrippa pressure and taxonomic coarse-graining / epistemic invisibility, with ongoing debate about whether the former is free-standing or the symptom of the latter.

With B held fixed JTB wants the J×T matrix:
* J T B = Knowledge
* J ¬T B = justified false belief
* ¬J T B = unjustified true belief
* ¬J ¬T B = unjustified false belief

On a strict K/B inventory the last three cells are forced into one undifferentiated Belief bin. Belief becomes the heterogeneous disjunction {J ¬T B, ¬J T B, ¬J ¬T B} and K ⊂ B. Justification and truth are therefore only difference-makers when they coincide in J∧T∧B.

1. Justification has no independent primitive and cannot be grounded non-circularly, non-regressively, non-dogmatically on a K/B only ontology.
K = B & T & J. A justifier for p must itself be an epistemic state, so it is K or B.
* If justification is cashed in Knowledge: to know p you must know q that justifies p, to know q you must know r that justifies q, etc. → Meno/Agrippa regress K p, K K p, K K K p..., circular grounding K justified by K, or arbitrary dogmatic stop.
* If justification is cashed in Belief: justification collapses into B1→B2→B3... with no terminating non-arbitrary factive ground. Halts are infinite regress, circularity or foundational dogmatism: properly basic beliefs accepted on fiat.

Hence J cannot be given an independent non-vicious foundation; it is either regressive/circular or terminates in ungrounded properly basic beliefs. This is the Agrippa/Münchhausen trilemma pressure.

2. Taxonomic coarse-graining / heterogeneity / invisibility of justification and truth outside the J∧T∧B cell.
With B held fixed the J×T matrix is as above. With only K vs B, the last three cells are forced into a single undifferentiated Belief bin.
Belief becomes the heterogeneous disjunction {justified false belief, unjustified true belief, unjustified false belief} and K ⊂ B, making knowledge a species of belief contrary to factivity.
* Justified false belief is lost: a warranted error is indistinguishable from an unwarranted error; justificatory merit is invisible outside the true case.
* Unjustified true belief is lost: a lucky/accidental true belief is indistinguishable from false belief; truth-by-luck is invisible outside the justified case.

Thus the system cannot say why a non-knowledge belief fails to be knowledge – failure can be falsity with justification, truth without justification, or both – and justification/truth are only trackable together in the coincident case of Knowledge. This is the classic demand for an intermediate state such as justified belief / true belief distinct from both mere belief and knowledge.

reflection_text.6:
The question is to name the two classic pre-Gettier problems for JTB when only epistemic kinds are Knowledge and Belief.

Current consensus after round 3 is essentially two interlocking failures, with ongoing nuance on emphasis and phrasing.

1. Justification has no independent, non-vicious ground in a K/B only ontology → Agrippa/Münchhausen trilemma / grounding problem.
K = B ∧ T ∧ J. With only K and B available a justifier for p must be a K-state or a B-state.
* Cashed in Knowledge: to know p you must know q that justifies p, to know q you must know r..., K p, K K p, K K K p..., Meno/Agrippa infinite regress, or circular grounding K justified by K, or arbitrary dogmatic stop.
* Cashed in Belief: justification collapses into belief justifying belief, B1→B2→B3..., no factive anchor, justification becomes vacuous or trivial, halting requires properly basic beliefs accepted on fiat.
Colleagues 5,6,10,11,12 treat this as a distinct grounding failure: J is either regressive/circular/dogmatic or vacuous and never gets an independent non-primitive foundation. Colleagues 1,7,12 argue the regress pressure is the symptom of the taxonomic collapse; once J has nowhere except K or B to live, cashing it in K gives knowledge-of-knowledge and cashing it in B makes justification just more belief. No disagreement on Gettier exclusion.

2. Coarse-graining / heterogeneity / epistemic invisibility of justification and truth outside the JT coincidence.
With B held fixed J×T matrix is:
J T B = Knowledge
J ¬T B = justified false belief
¬J T B = unjustified true belief
¬J ¬T B = unjustified false belief
With only Knowledge vs Belief the last three cells must be forced into a single undifferentiated Belief bin.
Hence Belief = { justified false, unjustified true, unjustified false } is heterogeneous and K ⊂ B.
* Justified false belief is erased. A warranted error is not knowledge because T fails, but is epistemically good in J. On K/B it must be called mere Belief and is conflated with unjustified false belief, so justificatory merit disappears outside the true case.
* Unjustified true belief is erased. A lucky/accidental true belief is not knowledge because J fails, but is true. On K/B it must be called mere Belief and is conflated with justified false and unjustified false belief, so truth-by-luck disappears.
Consequence: justification and truth are only trackable together in Knowledge; you cannot say why a non-knowledge belief fails to be knowledge – failure of T with J, J with T, or both are indistinguishable. Knowledge is rendered a species of belief, counter-intuitive given factivity.
Colleagues 1,2,3,4,8,10,11,12 articulate this as loss of distinct Justified Belief / True Belief states, justification invisibility, collapse of taxonomy. Some frame it as justification invisibility/coarse-graining, others as K being a species of B / heterogeneity.

Unresolved nuance remains on phrasing of the second problem and on the status of the regress: whether regress/dogmatism is a free-standing problem or the symptom of the taxonomic collapse. No disagreement that the two classic pre-Gettier costs are the grounding/ Agrippa pressure and the loss of independent J and T marks / heterogeneous Belief with erasure of justified false belief and unjustified true belief. Next step is to give precise names for the two problems: regress/dogmatism vs collapse/heterogeneity.

* ¬J T B = unjustified true belief
* ¬J ¬T B = unjustified false belief
On a strict Knowledge/Belief inventory the last three cells are forced into one undifferentiated Belief bin. Belief becomes the heterogeneous disjunction {J ¬T B, ¬J T B, ¬J ¬T B} and K ⊂ B. Justification and truth are only difference-makers when they coincide in J∧T∧B.

2.text:
With B held fixed JTB wants an independent J×T matrix

* J T B = Knowledge
* J ¬T B = justified false belief
* ¬J T B = unjustified true belief
* ¬J ¬T B = unjustified false belief

On a strict Knowledge / Belief inventory the three non-K cells are forced into one undifferentiated Belief bin. Belief becomes the heterogeneous disjunction {J ¬T B, ¬J T B, ¬J ¬T B} and K ⊂ B. Justification and truth are then only difference-makers in the conjunction J∧T∧B.

That two-state restriction produces two pre-Gettier costs.

1. Coarse-graining / epistemic invisibility of J and T outside the J∧T coincidence; loss of independent granularity and heterogeneity of Belief.

* Justified false belief is erased. A belief can be fully warranted by good evidence and still be false. JTB says it is not knowledge because T fails but it is epistemically good in J. On K/B it must be called mere Belief and is conflated with unjustified false belief and with unjustified true belief. Justificatory merit of a warranted error is invisible outside the true case.
* Unjustified true belief is erased. A belief can be true by luck, guess or coincidence without warrant. JTB says it is not knowledge because J fails but it is true. On K/B it also has to be called mere Belief and is conflated with justified false belief and unjustified false belief. Truth-by-luck is invisible outside the justified case.

A non-knowledge belief can now fail to be knowledge for three indistinguishable reasons – false but justified, true but unjustified, false and unjustified – all collapsed into “mere Belief”. That is the demand for an intermediate state Justified Belief / True Belief between mere Belief and Knowledge.

2. Justification has no independent, non-vicious home on a K/B ontology; the Agrippa/Münchhausen grounding pressure.

A justifier for p must itself be an epistemic state, i.e. K or B.

* Cashed in Knowledge: to know p you must know q that justifies p, to know q you must know r that justifies q, etc. Kp → KKp → KKKp… Meno/Agrippa infinite regress of higher-order knowledge, or closure by circular grounding K justified by K, or an arbitrary dogmatic stop.
* Cashed in Belief: justification collapses into B1 justifies B2 justifies B3… with no factive anchor.

The chain can only be halted by infinite regress, circularity or dogmatic foundationalism: basic beliefs taken as justified by fiat. J is therefore either regressive/circular/vacuous or terminates in brute belief; it cannot be given a non-circular, non-regressive, non-dogmatic foundation and has no primitive place to live distinct from K and B. This grounding pressure is the formal expression of the coarse-graining above: once justification has nowhere except K or B to live it becomes epistemically invisible except in its conjunction with truth in Knowledge.

1.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I think the framing that Colleagues 1, 12, 7 and 3 have been developing gets the question right once we separate a generic Agrippa grounding worry from the damage that is specific to a Knowledge/Belief only inventory.

With B held fixed JTB is meant to track the J × T matrix:
* J T B = Knowledge
* J ¬T B = justified false belief
* ¬J T B = unjustified true belief
* ¬J ¬T B = unjustified false belief

If the only names we have are Knowledge and Belief, the three non-K cells are forced into one undifferentiated Belief bin. Belief becomes the heterogeneous disjunction {J ¬T B, ¬J T B, ¬J ¬T B} and K ⊂ B. Justification and truth are then only difference-makers when they coincide in Knowledge.

That restriction creates two concrete, ontology-relative losses pre-Gettier.

First, justified false belief is erased. A belief can be fully warranted by good evidence and still be false. JTB says it is not knowledge because T fails, but it is epistemically good on the J dimension. On a K/B dichotomy it must be called mere Belief and is conflated with unjustified false belief and with unjustified true belief. The justificatory merit of a warranted error disappears; you can no longer mark a belief as better because it is justified even though false.

Second, unjustified true belief is erased. A belief can be true by luck, guess or coincidence without warrant. JTB says it is not knowledge because J fails, but it is true. On a K/B dichotomy it must be called mere Belief and is conflated with unjustified false belief and with unjustified true belief. reflection_text.2:
The discussion has stabilized around a two-cell taxonomy forced by a Knowledge/Belief only ontology under JTB with B held fixed.

JTB wants the J×T matrix on belief:
* J T B = Knowledge
* J ¬T B = justified false belief
* ¬J T B = unjustised true belief
* ¬J ¬T B = unjustified false belief

With only K/B labels the three non-K cells collapse into one Belief bin: Belief = {J¬TB, ¬JT B, ¬J¬TB}, K ⊂ B. Justification and truth are difference-makers only in the conjunction J∧T∧B.

Two pre-Gettier ontology-relative costs are consistently reported, with ongoing framing disagreement about priority.

1. Coarse-graining / epistemic invisibility of J and T outside J∧T; heterogeneity of Belief and loss of intermediate states.
* Justified false belief is erased. A fully warranted error is not Knowledge because T fails but is epistemically good in J. On K/B it must be called mere Belief and is conflated with unjustified false belief and unjustified true belief. Justificatory merit is invisible outside the true case.
* Unjustified true belief is erased. A lucky/accidental true guess is not Knowledge because J fails but is true. On K/B it is also mere Belief and is conflated with justified false belief and unjustified false belief. Truth-by-luck is invisible outside the justified case.
Hence a non-knowledge belief can fail to be knowledge for three indistinguishable reasons - false but justified, true but unjustified, false and unjustified - all collapsed into “mere Belief”. This is the demand for intermediate states Justified Belief / True Belief between mere Belief and Knowledge. Belief becomes a heterogeneous disjunction and K is a species of B, counter to factivity.

2. Justification has no independent, non-vicious home on a K/B ontology; Agrippa/Münchhausen grounding pressure for J.
A justifier for p must be an epistemic state, i.e. K or B.
* Cashed in Knowledge: to know p you must know q that justifies p → Kp, KKp, KKKp… Meno/Agrippa infinite regress of higher-order knowledge, or circular grounding K justified by K, or arbitrary dogmatic stop.
* Cashed in Belief: justification collapses into B1 justifies B2 justifies B3… belief-justifying-belief with no factive anchor.
J is therefore infinitely deferred, circularly self-supporting, vacuous, or terminates in brute belief; it cannot be given a non-circular, non-regressive, non-dogmatic primitive foundation distinct from K and B.

Relationship / disagreement: Colleagues 1,7,12 and parts of 3,7 stress that the Agrippa pressure is the symptom of the collapse, i.e. the distinctive ontology-relative damage is the taxonomic coarse-graining that erases justified false belief and unjustified true belief; circularity and dogmatism are just ways of closing the regress, not a second free-standing problem. For practical reporting the two are kept together as the pre-Gettier problems; no Gettier considerations included. Unresolved tension is merely terminological: whether to describe the damage as primarily taxonomic erasure with Agrippa as symptom, or as two interlocking costs.

2. Taxonomic coarse-graining / epistemic invisibility of J and T outside J∧T∧B / heterogeneity of Belief. With B held fixed JTB wants the J×T matrix; on K/B the last three cells are forced into one Belief bin.
* Justified false belief is erased. A warranted error is not knowledge because T fails but is epistemically good in J. On K/B it must be called mere Belief and is conflated with unjustified false belief and unjustified true belief, justificatory merit invisible outside the true case.
* Unjustified true belief is erased. A lucky/accidental true guess is not knowledge because J fails but is true. On K/B it also must be called mere Belief and is conflated with justified false belief and unjustified false belief, truth-by-luck invisible outside the justified case.

Hence justification and truth are only difference-makers when they coincide in Knowledge. The system can no longer say why a non-knowledge belief fails to be knowledge: failure of T with J, failure of J with T, or failure of both are indistinguishable as “mere Belief”.

Consensus remains that a distinct intermediate state — justified belief / warranted belief / true belief — is needed between mere Belief and Knowledge, and that the grounding problem and taxonomic loss are linked: once J has nowhere independent to live, cashing it out in K gives knowledge-of-knowledge and Agrippa, cashing it out in B makes justification just more belief, which is why the J×T matrix collapses.

reflection_text.4:
The discussion is now stabilised around two pre-Gettier difficulties for JTB when the epistemic inventory is restricted to Knowledge and Belief only, Gettier bracketed.

Shared formal frame: With B held fixed JTB wants the J×T matrix
* J T B = Knowledge
* J ¬T B = justified false belief
* ¬J T B = unjustified true belief
* ¬J ¬T B = unjustified false belief
On a strict K/B inventory the three non-K cells must be forced into one undifferentiated Belief bin. Belief becomes the heterogeneous disjunction {J ¬T B, ¬J T B, ¬J ¬T B} and K ⊂ B. Justification and truth are then only difference-makers when they coincide in Knowledge.

1. Justification has no independent, non-vicious home on a K/B ontology; Agrippa/Münchhausen grounding pressure.
A justifier for p must itself be an epistemic state, i.e. K or B.
* Cashed in Knowledge: to know p you must know q that justifies p, to know q you must know r... Kp, KKp, KKKp... Meno/Agrippa infinite regress of higher-order knowledge, or circular grounding K justified by K, or an arbitrary dogmatic stop at a belief known without prior justification.
* Cashed in Belief: justification collapses into B1 justifies B2 justifies B3... belief-justifying-belief with no factive anchor.
Halting is dogmatic foundationalism: basic beliefs taken as justified by fiat. J is therefore regressive/circular/vacuous or terminates in brute belief; it cannot be given a non-circular, non-regressive, non-dogmatic primitive foundation distinct from K and B.

2. Coarse-graining / heterogeneity of Belief and epistemic invisibility of Justification/Truth outside Knowledge; loss of the J×T matrix.
With only K vs B:
* Justified false belief is erased. A warranted error is not knowledge because T fails but is epistemically good in J. On K/B it must be called mere Belief and is conflated with unjustified false belief and unjustified true belief. Justificatory merit is invisible outside the true case.
* Unjustified true belief is erased. A lucky/accidental true guess is not knowledge because J fails but is true. On K/B it also has to be called mere Belief and is conflated with justified false belief and unjustified false belief. Truth-by-luck is invisible outside the justified case.
A non-knowledge belief can now fail to be knowledge for three indistinguishable reasons – false but justified, true but unjustified, false and unjustified – all collapsed into “mere Belief”. This forces the demand for an intermediate state such as Justified Belief / True Belief between mere Belief and Knowledge.

Unresolved nuance / disagreement in ordering:
Colleagues 1,12,7 frame the grounding pressure as the generic symptom of the ontology-relative collapse, and treat the distinctive damage as the taxonomic coarse-graining that erases justified false belief and unjustified true belief. Colleagues 10,11,2,3,4,6,8,9 list both as two concrete pre-Gettier costs, often presenting 1) Agrippa pressure and 2) coarse-graining/invisibility as co-equal. Core shared view remains that without a distinct justified-belief state JTB forces either an ungrounded justificatory chain and a K/B dichotomy that makes justification epistemically invisible, distinct from Gettier.
